Training Procedure Welcome to the Procify Developer Training. This section explains the overall structure of the course, how sessions are designed, and what is expected of you as a trainee. Read this before starting Session 1. Course Structure — 8 Sessions​ The training spans 8 sessions. Each session introduces a new layer of the platform — starting with setup and ending with publishing a fully working application. Sessions must be taken in order; each one builds directly on the previous. Session Topic Session 1 Platform Setup & Account Management Session 2 BOL — Entity Fundamentals & Initial Pages Session 3 Entity Configuration (Relations, Object Types, Status, ID Series) Session 4 Value Helps & Queries Session 5 BOL Logic & Validations with dashboard creation Session 6 Bindings, Navigation & Styling Session 7 Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour Session 8 Menu Configuration & App Management, Versioning & Publishing The Learn-by-Building Approach​ This training does not teach concepts in isolation. You will build one real application — a Customer complaint system — across all 89 sessions. Every concept is introduced exactly when you need it to make the next part of that application work. Why this matters for you You will always know WHY you are doing each step, not just HOW. By Session 8 you will have a working application demonstrating every major platform capability. The application grows session by session — if you miss a step it will affect later sessions. When you encounter a similar situation on a real project, you will have a concrete reference point from training.

Attend each session with the previous session's assignment completed and verified. Follow steps in this guide during hands-on time — do not skip ahead. Ask questions during the Review & Q&A phase, not during the trainer demonstration. The Application You Will Build This training guide uses a REAL application: the Customer complaints Application. You are not building a demo — you are building a production-ready application for delivery personnel. Every concept taught in every session is applied directly to build this application. By Session 9 you will have a fully working, published Delivery Agent Application.

Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, we will be able to: Understand the platform architecture. Create an application in the Workspace Hub. Define application roles and understand system vs. application roles. Create user accounts and assign them to an application with the correct role. Use Team Groups (User collections) to bundle multiple users and assign them to an application in a single, bulk step. Understands the role of data studio and page builder in application creation. ⚠ Why this session comes first The App you create today is built across ALL 9 sessions — treat it carefully. The Roles you define today are referenced in Session 5 (Validations) and Session 9 (Publishing access). The Users you create today are the test personas you will use to verify every screen built in Sessions 2–8. Part A — Understanding the Customer complaint Application​ Before touching any tool, you need a clear picture of the application you are building. Read this section carefully — every configuration decision in Sessions 1– traces back to this Business Requirement Document. Application Purpose​ The Customer Complaints Application is a solution designed to manage customer complaints end-to-end across three personas: • Log and track customer complaints with full lifecycle management. • Route complaints from Employee → Manager → Responsible Team. • Manage complaint line items, voice records, and file attachments. • Monitor escalations, SLA (TAT), and resolution timelines. • Provide dashboards per role so every user sees what they need. Application Roles — Three Personas​ This application defines exactly three application roles, each mapped to a Procify role-rollup level for viewable and UI-Auth controls: Role ID Business Name Procify Role Rollup Employee Complaint Creator Owner (s_role_rollup = 10) Manager Complaint Assignor Supervisor (s_role_rollup = 20) Responsible Team Issue Resolver Reviewer (s_role_rollup = 30) 📘 Role Precedence Rule Precedence is a number. Lower = higher priority. Employee: precedence 3, Manager: precedence 2, ResponsibleTeam: precedence 1. This means if a user has multiple roles, the lower-precedence number overrides. Your developer account should be assigned Manager (precedence 2) for full access during testing. Role Responsibilities​ Action Employee(Owner) Manager(Supervisor) Responsible Team(Reviewer) Create a new complaint ✅ Yes — — View own complaints ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Edit complaint description ✅ Yes (OPEN only) ✅ Yes — Assign responsible team — ✅ Yes — Move status → INPROCESS — ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Move status → ON HOLD — — ✅ Yes Move status → RESOLVED — ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Move status → CLOSED ✅ Yes ✅ Yes — Reopen a closed complaint ✅ Yes ✅ Yes — Add complaint items ✅ Yes (OPEN/INPROCESS) — — Add voice/comment records ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Upload attachments ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Escalate complaint ✅ Yes ✅ Yes — View all complaints (not just own) — ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (assigned) Entities to be Built​ Entity ID Primary Key Built in Session d_complaints complaint_id Session 1 d_complaint_item item_id Session 2 d_complaint_voices voice_id Session 2 d_complaints_attachment attachment_id Session 2 d_customers customer_id Session 2 d_resp_team emp_id Session 2 Complaint Status Flow​ The status lifecycle has 6 states. Each transition is triggered by a specific role: OPEN INPROCESS ON HOLD RESOLVED CLOSED REOPEN ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ Triggered by Employee Triggered by Manager / Responsible Team Triggered by Responsible Team Triggered by Responsible Team / Manager Triggered by Manager / Employee Triggered by Employee / Manager Status Badge Colour / Meaning OPEN Blue — complaint logged by Employee, awaiting Manager assignment INPROCESS Orange — Manager assigned responsible team; team working on it ON HOLD Purple — Responsible Team placed on hold pending information RESOLVED Green — Responsible Team marked as resolved CLOSED Grey — Manager confirmed resolution and closed the ticket REOPEN Red — Employee or Manager reopened a resolved/closed complaint 📘 Status Transition Rules OPEN → INPROCESS: only Manager can trigger (by assigning responsible_team).INPROCESS → ON HOLD / RESOLVED: only ResponsibleTeam can trigger.RESOLVED → CLOSED: only Manager can trigger.CLOSED → REOPEN: Employee or Manager can reopen; status resets to OPEN.ON HOLD → INPROCESS: only ResponsibleTeam can resume. d_complaint — Propertiesplaints — All Properties Property ID Data Type Key Attr Notes complaint_id String 🔑 PK Auto-generated via ID Series — e.g. CMP-00001 complaint_desc Text ❗ Mandatory Full description of the complaint customer_id String — FK → d_customers.customer_id priority String — Values: Low / Medium / High / Critical status string — Status of the ticket. first_response_date Timestamp — Date of first response to customer planned_resolution_date Timestamp — Planned closure date assigned_to String — Employee user ID who owns the complaint responsible_manager String — FK → d_sales_team.emp_id — Manager assigned responsible_team String — Team assigned by Manager for resolution remark Text — Internal remarks or resolution notes closed_on Timestamp — Date the complaint was closed is_escalated Boolean — Default: false — true if escalated by Manager complaint_type String — Type Part E — understanding the importance of Procify​ Every application starts the same way: someone hands a developer a requirements document and says 'build this.' The Customer complaints Application Business Requirement Document (BRD) you read in Session 1 defines exactly what data needs to be stored — 3 data objects, their fields, and their relationships. The first job as a developer is to turn those definitions into a working database schema. Before opening any tool, it is worth understanding what that process looks like — and how much of it Procify eliminates. The rest of this part walks through the traditional process step by step, then shows exactly which steps the data studio replaces. What Is a Schema?​ 📘 Schema — The Blueprint of Your Application's Data A schema is the complete definition of the data your application stores: what tables exist, what columns each table has, what type of data each column holds, and how tables relate to each other. The schema is the foundation of every application. Without it, there is no database. Without a database, there is no data. Without data, there is no application. Building the schema is always the first development task after reading a BRD. Everything else — APIs, Pages, logic — is built on top of it. In our BRD, the schema is already defined in Section 4 (Entity Relationship Overview). The 4 entities, their properties, and their relationships are all there. Our job today is to implement that schema. The Traditional Way of Building a Schema​ 🏗 How developers build a schema without a low-code platform Step 1 — Write SQL scripts: A backend developer writes CREATE TABLE statements for each entity. For the Delivery table alone, that is 12 columns — each with its SQL data type, constraints, default values, and indexes. Step 2 — Write an ORM model: For every SQL table, the developer writes a model class in the backend language (Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Java). This class mirrors the database table and handles object-relational mapping. Step 3 — Write REST API endpoints: For each entity, the developer writes GET, POST, PUT, DELETE API handlers. Each handler validates input, maps it to the model, executes the database query, and returns the response. Step 4 — Write validation logic: For each property that has rules (mandatory, unique, min/max), the developer writes validation code — either in the model or in the API handler. Step 5 — Handle database migrations: Every time the schema changes (new property, renamed column), the developer writes a migration script to alter the existing tables without losing data. Step 6 — Test the API: The developer uses Postman or writes unit tests to verify each endpoint returns the correct data in the correct format. Repeat for all 4 entities. 🔴 The pain of the traditional approach Multiple files across multiple layers — SQL files, model files, API controller files, test files. A change to one field requires edits in 4–6 places. Context switching: a single developer must switch between SQL, backend language, API design, and test writing — each requiring a different mental mode. Time cost: 3–4 days of developer time before a single screen can be shown to a stakeholder. Repetition: most of this work is identical boilerplate — every entity needs the same pattern of SQL + ORM + CRUD APIs. Nothing creative, just repetitive. ​ The Procify Way​ ✅ How Procifyreplaces the traditional schema-building process In Klobase, all 6 traditional steps are replaced by a single tool: the data studio. You define the entity (name, type) → add properties (name, data type, key attributes) → click Update Schema. Done. The platform automatically generates: the database table (SQL step 1), the data access layer (ORM step 2), the REST API endpoints (step 3), basic validation from key attributes (step 4), and handles schema updates automatically (step 5). There are no separate files to keep in sync. The data studio is the single source of truth. Everything downstream — API, data validation, mobile sync — is derived from it automatically. Time with Klobase: the same 4 entities, all properties, schema live in the database — approximately 2 hours in this session. The developer's time is freed for the parts that actually require thinking: business logic, UI design, user experience. This is not an approximation. Let us make it concrete: Traditional Task data studio Replacement Write CREATE TABLE SQL for Delivery entity Create entity in data studio — choose type, add properties, click Save Write ORM model class (12 fields × 4 entities) Already done — properties ARE the model Write 16+ REST API endpoints Already done — fireQuery apis are available to fetch data Write validation for mandatory fields Check the Mandatory key attribute icon on the property and validation will be handled by platform. Write database migration script Click Update Schema again — the platform handles ALTER TABLE automatically Test APIs with Postman Use the built-in Test function in the data studio toolbar ​ The Traditional Way of Building a UI​ 🔴 Traditional screen development requires five separate layers 1. HTML / JSX template — the visual structure: list container, card component, placeholder slots for each field. 2. CSS / styling — card appearance, status badge colours, spacing, responsiveness for mobile and desktop. 3. API call — GET /complaints?user={currentUser.id} to fetch complaint records from the server. 4. State management (React state, Redux, etc.) — store the fetched array, handle loading state, handle error state, trigger re-renders when data changes. 5. Data binding — map each complaint object's fields to the template slots: {complaint.complaint_desc}, {complaint.priority}. Total: 3–5 files, 150–300 lines of code, for one list screen. Any change to one layer often requires changes to the others. The Procify Way — The Page Wizard & Page Builder​ ✅ The Page Builder replaces all five layers with a single metadata configuration In the Page Builder you configure the screen structure. The platform reads your configuration and generates the visual rendering, handles all data fetching, manages state automatically, applies your styling choices, and wires up the data bindings. This means: one tool, no files to keep in sync, no merge conflicts on screen structure, no state management code. The Page Wizard (used in this session) gives you a ready-made screen in minutes. Session 2 teaches you to build the same screen step-by-step so you understand every level of the hierarchy. Pages configured in the Page Builder render identically on both browser (web) and mobile (KloTouch) — no separate mobile codebase needed. B.3 — The Page Hierarchy (UI Editor 7.0 User Guide — Sections 3.0–7.0)​ Every screen in Klobase follows a strict 5-level hierarchy. This is the most important structural concept in UI development. Each level has a mandatory naming convention prefix: 📘 Five-Level Page Hierarchy Level 1 — PAGE (prefix: p_) The root container. Holds all layouts. Created first. One page can have multiple layouts (one per device type). At runtime, the platform picks the layout based on device: screencontainerdesktop, screencontainermobile, screencontainertab, screencontainerdefault. Level 2 — PAGE LAYOUT (prefix: pl_) Sits directly under the Page. Defines HOW the page areas are arranged. screenType options: stack, tab, two_column, object_page, grid_layout, hsplitter, vsplitter. Example: pl_complaints_desk (two column layout for desktop). Level 3 — PAGE AREA (prefix: pa_) A logical sub-container inside the layout. Can itself have a screenType (tab, stack, splitter). Sections are assigned to page areas to determine WHERE they render. Example: pa_complaints (list area), pa_complaint_details (detail area). Level 4 — SECTION (prefix: s_) The rendering unit. screenType determines HOW it displays data. Types: search, cardlist, card, form, grid, tree, timeline, map, calendar. Must be assigned to a Page Area to appear in the UI. Example: s_search (search), s_complaints (grid), s_detail_header (form). Level 5 — CONTROLS Individual fields, buttons, labels, icons bound to entity properties. Added via: right-click section → New → Controls, OR drag from unused TransNode properties. Section screenType Renders As search Filter bar with Close / Reset / Search buttons. Auto-generates the search toolbar. cardlist List of records as card rows — one card per record. Good for mobile and compact lists. grid Tabular list with column headers and rows. Supports sort, filter, group-by per column. form Detail form layout. Each control renders as a labelled input field. card Single entity rendered as a CSS grid card. One record only. tab Used on Page Areas to group child sections as tabs. showTitle must be true for tab labels. tree Hierarchical tree display for nested data. B.4 — Page Data Model (TransNodes) — Concept​ The Page Data Model defines the data available to a screen. Every section and control that displays data must be bound to a TransNode. A TransNode is a “data pipe” — it fetches entity records from the database and makes them available to sections and controls on the page. Node Type Fetches EntitySet A LIST of records. Use for search sections, grids, card lists. Suffix convention: _list. Example: d_complaints_list Entity ONE record (the currently selected record). Use for detail forms. Suffix convention: _detail. Example: d_complaints_detail Query Records from a kloQuery with WHERE conditions, joins, sorting. Suffix convention: _query. Other Non-standard / custom use cases. 📘 Fold From — The Critical Link Between List and Detail When you create d_complaints_detail (Entity type) and set its “Fold From” = d_complaints_list, the platform automatically loads the selected record’s data into d_complaints_detail whenever the user clicks a row in the list. This is the mechanism that connects list → detail. Without Fold From: the detail section will always be empty. With Fold From: clicking any complaint row in the list instantly populates the detail form. TransNode naming convention (from UI Editor 7.0 Guide): EntitySet → _list suffix Entity → _detail suffix Query → _query suffix B.5 — Target Screen Design for p_complaints​ Based on the Customer Complaints Application design, the p_complaints page has two page areas. The complete target structure is: | 📘 p_complaints — Full Page Structure PAGE: p_complaints └─ pl_complaints_desk (PageLayout — screenType: two column) ├─ pa_complaints (PageArea 1 — List Panel) | ├─ s_search (Section — screenType: search) | | Controls: ticket_id, desc, customer_id, responsible_tea, priority, | | s_status, is_escalated, cust_category, cust_type, | | complaint_type, raised_by, state, nature_of_compl, actual_tat, standard_tat | └─ s_complaints (Section — screenType: grid) | Controls: ticket_id (link), customer_id, priority, s_status, | planned_res_dat, closed_on, sales_manager └─ pa_complaint_details (PageArea 2 — Tab) ├─ section_toolbar (Action toolbar: Edit/Save/Add buttons) ├─ s_detail_header (Section — screenType: card— key fields) | Controls: desc, i_ageing, t_ageing, s_status, i_t_priority, i_res_team, responsible_tea └─ pa_comp_details (PageArea — screenType: default) ├─ s_complaint_details ├─ s_complaint_details3 → form ├─ s_complaint_details5 ├─ s_reporter_details —> form ├─ s_complaint_details2 ├─ s_complaint_details4 → form | | :---- | B.6 — Step 1: Create the Page (p_complaints)​ 1 Open Page Builder from Design Studio → Page Builder. Select your application from the app dropdown. 2 Click the Edit icon in the toolbar to enable edit mode. 3 Click the + icon → Create Blank Page. 4 Page ID: p_complaints 5 The page appears in the tree. No layouts yet — proceed to Step 2. ![][image3] B.7 — Step 2: Create the Page Layout (pl_complaints_desk)​ The Page Layout sits directly under the Page and defines the arrangement type for all page areas. According to UI Editor 7.0 Guide (Section 4.0): at runtime only one pageLayout is picked based on the device type — determined by the page’s screencontainerdefault, screencontainerdesktop, etc. properties. 1 In the tree, right-click on p_complaints → New → Page Layout. A new layout is added to the tree. 2 Right-click the new layout → Rename → enter: pl_complaints_desk. Press Enter. 3 Click pl_complaints_desk in the tree to open its Detail panel on the right. 4 In the Detail panel, set screenType = two column. This renders all assigned page areas one after another — the standard layout for list+detail screens. 5 Now click on p_complaints in the tree. In its Detail panel, set screencontainerdefault = pl_complaints_desk. This tells the platform: use this layout on all devices unless a device-specific layout is set. 6 Save. 📘 Layout Type Quick Reference (UI Editor 7.0 Guide — Section 12.0) stack — Sections / areas render one after another vertically. One subscreen shown at a time. two_column — Master-detail split: left panel (list) + right panel (detail). Max 2 columns. tab — Renders children as tabbed panels. Used at Page Area level for detail tabs. object_page — SAP-style object page: sticky header + tab body sections. hsplitter — Horizontal split with resizable rows. vsplitter — Vertical split with resizable columns. grid_layout / css_grid — CSS Grid-based placement. Requires modeller configuration. B.8 — Step 3: Configure the Page Data Model (TransNodes)​ Select p_complaints in the tree. Click the Page Data Model icon (right panel tab). Click + to add Model Paths. Create the two root TransNodes: 1 Click + in the Page Data Model panel. Dialog opens. 2 Node Path : search 3 Click Transfer&Link of search. Node Path: list 4 Click Transfer&Link of list Node Path: detail 5 Save. These two TransNodes are the data backbone for all sections on this page. B.9 — Step 4: Create the List Page Area (pa_complaints)​ Per UI Editor 7.0 Guide (Section 5.0): The Page Area is the next level after Page Layout. Page Areas are embedded with the Page Layout via the Layout Data assignment. 1 Right-click on pl_complaints_desk → New → Page Area. A new page area is added. 2 Right-click the new page area → Rename → pa_complaints. 4 Save. B.9.1 — Creating the Search Section (s_search)​ Per UI Editor 7.0 Guide (Section 6.1): To add a new section, right-click on the page area and select New → Section. The search screenType auto-generates the filter bar with Close / Reset / Search buttons. 1 Right-click on pa_complaints → New → Section. Rename it: s_search. 2 In the Detail panel, set screenType = search. 4 Select s_search in the tree. In the Detail panel, set the TransNode (path) = search. 5 Add controls: right-click s_search →click New in poup → Controls . OR go to the Page Data Model panel → select search→ Unused Properties tab → drag properties directly to s_search in the tree. 6 Add all controls as listed in the note below. Save after each set. 📘 s_search Controls — Match the Search Bar in the Screenshot Row 1: complaint_id (Ticket Id text input), s_status, complaint_type Row 2: desc (Description text input), is_escalated (Escalated checkbox), nature_of_compl Row 3: customer_id (Employee ID — with Value Help picker icon), cust_category (Employee, actual_tat (Actual TAT number input) Row 4: priority, cust_type , standard_tat (Standard TAT number input) Tree also shows: raised_by, state, cust_category_lbl, cust_type_lbl (label controls for display) How to add controls via drag-and-drop (UI Editor 7.0 Guide — Section 2.2.6 DnD on Preview): 1. In the Page Data Model panel, select search→ click Unused Properties tab. 2. Drag any property from the unused list and drop it onto s_search in the tree. 3. The control is created automatically with the property binding pre-set. 4. You can drag and drop controls within the section to align the controls. 📸 Final Output — After Creating s_search Once s_search is created with all controls and you click Show Full Preview, you will see the search filter bar rendered at the top of the screen exactly as shown below. Expected output: s_search renders the Employee Complaints filter bar with all fields — Ticket Id, Status, Complaint Type, Escalated checkbox, Employee Category, Priority, Nature of Complaint, Actual TAT, and Standard TAT. Close / Reset / Search buttons are auto-generated by the search scr eenType. 📸 Tree View — How s_search Looks in the Page Builder Tree After adding all controls, s_search in the tree should look like the screenshot below. Each control is listed under the section with its entity property binding. Page Builder tree showing pa_complaints → s_search with all controls: ticket_id, desc, customer_id, responsible_tea, priority, s_status, is_escalated, cust_category_lbl, cust_category, cust_type_lbl, cust_type, complaint_type, raised_by, state, nature_of_compl, actual_tat, standard_tat B.9.2 — Creating the Complaints List Section (s_complaints)​ The grid section renders complaint records as rows with sortable, filterable columns. Per UI Editor 7.0 Guide (Section 6.2 — Grid): For desktop view, section screenType should be “grid”. Add a conf_grid000 config node for grid behaviour settings. 1 Right-click pa_complaints → New → Section. Rename: s_complaints. 2 In the Detail panel, set screenType = grid. 3 Set TransNode path = list. 4 Right-click pa_complaints → New → Assign → select s_complaints (below s_search). Save. 5 Add controls from d_complaints_list TransNode unused properties: ticket_id (set the control type as m.link and add press event with function as ‘navTo’(Fill the sunscreen id as detail page area) ), customer_id, priority, s_status, planned_res_dat, closed_on, sales_manager. 6 Right-click s_complaints → New → Config → rename: conf_grid000. This config node stores grid behaviour properties. 7 Right-click s_complaints → New → Toolbar. Add Add and Delete buttons in the toolbar detail. 8 Arrange the controls in s_complaints by using drag and drop feature inside section 9 Save. 📸 Final Output — After Creating s_complaint Once s_complaints is created with all controls and you click Show Full Preview, you will see the complaints list rendered below search section You can notice that the screen we created is not the same in the provided screenshot. Complaint_id contains id-desc Status has color Grid is occupying full screen Pont 1 & 2 will be achieved in the upcoming sessions. For point 3 we can achieve this by setting screentype of pa_complaints as fit_to_area and mark auto_height as true for s_complaints layout. 📸 Tree View — How s_complaints Looks in the Page Builder Tree After building s_complaints, it should appear in the tree as shown below — with ticket_id as a navigation link, all property controls, conf_grid000, and section_toolbar. Page Builder tree showing s_complaints with controls: ticket_id (link icon), customer_id, priority, s_status, planned_res_dat, closed_on, sales_manager, plus conf_grid000 config and section_toolbar B.10 — Step 5: Create the Detail Page Area (pa_complaint_details)​ The detail area loads when a complaint row is selected from the list. It contains a toolbar for actions, a header section showing critical fields, and a tabbed area for all complaint details. 1 Right-click pl_complaints_desk → New → Page Area. Rename: pa_complaint_details. 2 Update screentype as tab B.10.2 — Creating the Detail Header Section (s_detail_header)​ The header section displays the most critical complaint fields prominently. screenType: card. Bound to d_complaints_detail TransNode. 1 Right-click pa_complaint_details → New → Section. Rename: s_detail_header. 2 Set screenType = card. Set TransNode path = detail. 3 Add controls from d_complaints_detail unused properties: desc, s_status, priority, res_team, responsible_tea. ⇒ change the control to m.Text for making it readable only 4 Save. 📸 Final Output — After Creating s_detail_header Once s_detail_header is created with all controls and you click Show Full Preview, you will see the result as mentioned below after modeling which will be covered in upcoming sessions 📸 Tree View — How s_detail_header Looks in the Page Builder Tree After creating s_detail_header with all header controls, it should appear as shown below. Page Builder tree showing s_detail_header with controls: desc, i_ageing (icon), t_ageing (text), s_status, i_t_priority (priority icon), i_res_team (team icon), responsible_tea B.10.3 — Creating the Detail Area (pa_comp_details)​ pa_comp_details is a nested Page Area inside pa_complaint_details. 1 Right-click page area→ New → Page Area. Rename: pa_comp_details. 2 In the Detail panel, set screenType = default. Set showTitle = true & title = detail so tab labels are visible. 3 Assign the page area to pa_complaints_detail. 4 Now create all 4 sections inside pa_comp_details. Right-click pa_comp_details → New → Section for each. Set each to screenType = form Set TransNode = detail for form sections. 5 Set each section’s title property — this becomes the tab label visible at runtime. 5 Assign all 4 sections to pa_comp_details in the correct sequence. Save. 6 Set type = header for s_detail_header layout & type = section for pa_comp_details. 7 Set press event for complaint_id link with function as navTo => pageArea : pa_complaint_details. Section ID Screen Type Tab Title / Contents s_complaint_details form Complaint Details — complaint_id, complaint_type, description, priority, status, customer_id s_assigment_details form Assignment — responsible_team, manager, first response date, planned resolution date s_timeline_details form TAT & Timeline — actual_tat, standard_tat, closed_on, created_on, modified_on s_admin_info form Contains s_created_by, s_modified_by, s_created_on and s_modified_on B.10.3 — Add Action buttons for pa_comp_details​ 1 Right-click pa_comp_details→ New → Toolbar. 2 Set showAdd and ShowDelete = false 3 Right-click section-Toolbar → New → Action/Button. 4 Right-click button01 → rename → edit 5 Set text = Edit 6 Repeat steps 3,4 and 5 for save with this.saveTransaction("Data saved successfully.", "Save Failed.", true, true) 7 Repeat steps 3,4 and 5 for cancel with this.refreshTransnode("complaints_detail","DISPLAY",true) 📸 Final Output — After Creating pa_comp_details 📸 Tree View — How pa_complaint_details Looks After Full Setup Page Builder tree showing pa_complaint_details with: section_toolbar, s_detail_header, and nested pa_comp_details containing all 7 tab sections — s_complaint_details, s_complaint_details3, s_complaint_details5, s_reporter_details, s_complaint_details2, s_complaint_details4, s_complaint_item B.11 — Step 6: Preview and Verify the Complete Screen​ 1 Save all changes in the Page Builder. 2 Click Show Full Preview. The screen loads with live complaint data from the database. 3 Verify the search bar appears at the top: Ticket Id, Status, Complaint Type, Escalated, Employee Category, Priority fields visible. Close / Reset / Search buttons present. 4 Verify the complaint list appears below the search bar with columns: ticket_id (clickable link), customer_id, priority, status, planned resolution date, closed date. 5 Click a complaint row. Verify the detail area loads with the header section (description, status, priority) and the tab area below. 6 Navigate through each tab — Complaint Details, Assignment, Reporter Info, TAT & Timeline, Complaint Items. Verify correct fields in each. 7 If a section appears blank: select it in the tree and check that its TransNode path is correctly set in the Detail panel. Ensure Fold From is set on d_complaints_detail. ✔ UI Build Checkpoint — Verify Before Session 3 p_complaints page created with pl_complaints_desk as default layout. Page Data Model has d_complaints_list (EntitySet) and d_complaints_detail (Entity, Fold From: list). pa_complaints: s_search (search, all filter fields) + s_complaints (grid, 7 columns incl. navigation link). pa_complaint_details: section_toolbar + s_detail_header (form, header fields) + pa_comp_details (tab). pa_comp_details: 7 tab sections including s_complaint_item (grid) for complaint line items. Full Preview shows the search bar — exact match with the reference screenshots from the trainer. Clicking a complaint row loads the detail area with all tabs populated.

documents.t: By the end of this session, you will be able to: Understand what Entity Relations are and create Primary and Non-Primary (Aggregated) relations between entities. Understand what Object Types are, why they are needed, and configure complaint type classifications for d_complaints. Configure Status and Status Groups to represent the complaint lifecycle (OPEN → INPROCESS → ON HOLD → RESOLVED → CLOSED → REOPEN). Set up an ID Series for complaint_id to auto-generate readable complaint numbers (e.g. CMP-00001). Update the p_complaints UI to reflect the new entity configuration — making the complaint_type, status, and complaint_id fields work correctly in the page. 📘 What This Session Builds On Session 1 created the application, roles, users, and d_complaints entity with raw properties. Session 2 created the remaining 5 entities and built the full p_complaints page step by step. Session 3 enriches the d_complaints entity with the platform features that turn raw fields into intelligent, lifecycle-aware data. After Session 3, the complaint_id will auto-generate, the status dropdown will show the correct lifecycle values, and complaint_type will be classified. Without a relation defined in the BOL Editor, the platform has no way to automatically load child records when a parent record is selected — and no way to bundle the BO for save/delete operations. There are two types of relations in Klobase: Relation Type What It Means Primary Relation Tight parent-child bond WITHIN the same Business Object (BO). A child entity is dependent on the parent. Prefixed pr_. Used for d_complaint_item, d_complaint_voices, d_complaints_attachment — all children of d_complaints. Non-Primary (Aggregated) Relation Looser link BETWEEN BOs. Used to reference standalone master entities. Prefixed r_. Used for d_customers and d_resp_team which are independent master entities. 📘 Why Relations Matter in the UI When a relation is defined and referenced in a TransNode in the Page Builder, the platform automatically fetches the child/linked entity records when the parent record is loaded. Without a relation, you would have to write manual queries and wire up the data fetch yourself. The TransNode type 'Relation' in the Page Data Model uses the relation name defined here — this is why naming the relation correctly matters. Naming convention (from BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Best Practices): pr_ prefix for primary relations, r_ prefix for associated/aggregated relations. Always lowercase. A.2 — Relations to Create for d_complaints​ You will create 5 relations on the d_complaints root entity — one for each related entity. Relation ID Type Return Entity Cardinality r_complaint_item Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_complaint_item 1:n (One complaint → Many items) r_complaint_voices Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_complaint_voices 1:n (One complaint → Many voices) r_complaint_attach Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_complaints_attachment 1:n (One complaint → Many attachments) r_customer Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_customers 1:1 (One complaint has one customer) r_resp_team Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_resp_team 1:1 (One complaint has one responsible team member) A.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Primary Relation​ Primary Relation will be automatically created with the creation of child entity and requires no manual action A.4 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Non-Primary (Aggregated) Relation​ Non-primary relations link d_complaints to standalone master entities (d_customers and d_resp_team). Follow these steps for r_customer # Action Detail 1 d_complaints Relations tab click d_complaints in the tree and go back to the Relations tab. 2 Click Add Click the Add (+) icon to add a new relation row. 3 Fill Relation Details Relation Name: r_customer 4 Configure Mapping Click Mapping. Add: Source Property = customer_id 5 Save Click Save. 💡 Mapping Type — BOTH Explained ON CREATE: When a new d_complaint_item is created under a d_complaints parent, the platform automatically copies the complaint_id value into the ticket_id field of the new item. You never have to set this manually. ON QUERY: When you query d_complaint_item records for a given complaint, the platform uses ticket_id = complaint_id as the WHERE condition automatically. BOTH: Use this for standard parent-child relations — it handles both the create and the fetch scenarios. Now repeat the same steps to create the remaining relations: Relation ID Return Entity Mapping (Source → Target) r_complaint_voices d_complaint_voices complaint_id → ticket_id r_complaint_items d_complaint_item complaint_id → ticket_id r_complaint_attach d_complaints_attachment complaint_id → complaint_id r_resp_team d_resp_team responsible_team → emp_id Part B — Configuring Object Types for d_complaints​ B.1 — What Is an Object Type?​ In Klobase, an Object Type (stored in the system property s_object_type) is a classification that tags each record as belonging to a specific type. Object Types serve two important purposes: They enable role-based visibility: a button or field can be made visible/editable only for a specific role AND a specific object type combination. This is used for screen behavior in Session 7. They allow ID Series to be object-type-specific: a different number series prefix can be applied per object type — for example, complaints created by Maventic employees might use a different prefix than those created by Procify employees. 📘 Object Type vs Object Group Object Group is a container that groups related Object Types together. The group is used as the filter boundary. Object Type is the actual tag applied to individual records (e.g. MAVENTIC, PROCIFY). Every Object Type must belong to exactly one Object Group. For the Customer Complaints application: Object Group = company_types Object Types = MAVENTIC, PROCIFY Best Practice (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide): Always maintain an Object Group to group types — the same group can be used in default filters based on users. B.2 — Object Types for d_complaints​ Object Type ID Description MAVENTIC Complaints created by Maventic employees PROCIFY Complaints created by Procify employees B.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating Object Group and Object Types​ # Action Detail 1 Go to Object Type tab Select d_complaints in the tree. Click the Object Type tab in the Detail panel. The tab shows two sections: the upper section for Object Types 2 Open Object Group dialog In the Object Type section, click the dialog icon next to the Object Group field to open the Object Group management dialog. 3 Create Object Group In the Object Group dialog, click Add. Fill in: Object Group ID: complaint_types 4 Close dialog Click Cancel / Close on the Object Group dialog to return to the Object Type tab. 5 Add first Object Type Fill: Object Type: MAVENTIC 6 Add remaining types Repeat Add for: PROCIFY — under Object Group: complaint_types. Click Save after all are added. 7 Verify All Object Types appear in the list, all with Object Group: complaint_types. ​ After adding the object type to differentiate complaints based on company is only half in order to achieve difference in complaint_id based on company another part is pending which is configuring ID Series based on object_type. Part C — Setting Up ID Series for Auto-Numbering​ D.1 — What Is an ID Series?​ An ID Series is a platform-managed counter that automatically generates primary key values when a new record is created. Without an ID Series on complaint_id, a developer would need to generate unique IDs manually — which is error-prone and cannot produce readable, formatted numbers like CMP-00001. ID Series Type Description Auto Number Returns an incrementing number. Combined with a Prefix pattern to produce CMP-00001, CMP-00002, etc. GUID Returns a 32-character UUID. Good for distributed offline scenarios. Not human-readable. None No auto-generation. The developer or rule must set the key manually. D.2 — ID Series to Configure​ Property Type Company Pattern/Prefix Start From complaint_id Auto Number PROCIFY Prefix: P- (generates P-00001) 1 complaint_id Auto Number MAVENTIC Prefix: M - (generates M-00001) 1 D.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating the ID Series​ # Action Detail 1 Select d_complaints In the Data Studio tree, click on d_complaints. 2 Go to Properties tab Click the Properties tab in the Detail panel. Locate the complaint_id property row. 3 Open ID Series Click the navigation right arrow (→) at the end of the complaint_id row. The ID Series dialog opens for this property. 4 Click Add Click the Add (+) icon in the ID Series dialog. A new entry row appears. 5 Fill ID Series details ID: idp_complaint 6 Click Add Click the Add (+) icon in the ID Series dialog. A new entry row appears. 7 Fill ID Series details ID: idm_complaint 8 Close dialog Click Close on the dialog. The ID Series entry is saved. 9 Save Click Save in the Data Studio toolbar. The complaint_id property now has an ID Series configured. 📘 ID Series Fields Reference (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.1 Creating ID Series) ID: Unique ID of the series. Naming convention: id_ prefix, all lowercase. Example: id_complaint. Type: Auto Number = incremental counter. Most common for business records. From: Starting number for the series. Use 1 to start from P-00001. Prefix: Text prepended before the number. P- produces P-1, P-2, etc. Chunk Size: Default 100. The server pre-allocates this many IDs per session (important for offline apps). Scope: Global (default) — one counter shared across all users and tenants. Pattern: Can be used to produce complex formats. For simple prefix + number, just use the Prefix field. D.4 — Testing the ID Series​ # Action Detail 1 Open Data Browser With d_complaints selected, click Test in the toolbar. The Data Browser opens. 2 Create a new record Click Add (+ Execute → Add → select object_type). Leave complaint_id blank — the platform will fill it. 3 Fill minimal fields complaint_desc: Test auto-number 4 Verify The complaint_id column should show P-00001 for Procify and M-0001 for Maventic (or the next available number). If it shows a blank or an error, revisit the ID Series configuration. Part C — Configuring Status and Status Groups​ C.1 — What Is Status in Klobase?​ The system property s_status represents the current state of a complaint record. The Status tab in the Data Studio lets you define the allowed values for s_status and group them into Status Groups. Status Groups are named collections of statuses. They are used in Vienable (Session 7) to control screen behaviour: for example, the Edit button is visible only when s_status is in the OPEN_GROUP, and the Assign Team button is visible only when s_status is in the INPROCESS_GROUP. 📘 Status Lifecycle for Customer Complaints The complaint lifecycle defined in the BRD has 6 states: OPEN → INPROCESS → ON_HOLD / RESOLVED → CLOSED / REOPEN Each status transition is triggered by a specific role (defined in the Role Responsibility matrix from Session 1 Part A). In this session you define the status values and groups. The actual UI enforcement of transitions using Vienable happens in Session 7. C.2 — Status Values and Groups to Configure​ Status ID Short Label Status Group Triggered By OPEN Open OPEN Auto-set on complaint creation by Employee INPROCESS In Process INPROCESS Manager assigns responsible_team ON_HOLD On Hold INPROCESS Responsible Team puts on hold RESOLVED Resolved ACCEPTED Responsible Team / Manager marks resolved CLOSED Closed COMPLETED Manager confirms resolution and closes REOPEN Re-Opened OPEN Employee or Manager reopens a closed complaint C.3 — Step-by-Step: Adding Status Values​ # Action Detail 1 Go to Status tab Select d_complaints in the tree. Click the Status tab in the Detail panel. 2 Enable Switch on the status and click save and edit 3 Add OPEN status Click the Add Record(+) icon. Fill: Status: OPEN 4 Add remaining statuses Repeat Add for each status: INPROCESS (In Process), ON_HOLD (On Hold), RESOLVED (Resolved), CLOSED (Closed), REOPEN (Re-Opened) for PROCIFY. Click Save after all are added. Repeat for MAVENTIC Repeat the Action 3 and 4 for object_type maventic as well. 4 Verify list All 12 status values appear in the status list. 💡 Why Status Groups Are Important for This Application Session 7 will use these groups to configure Vienable on buttons and fields. Example: The 'Edit' button will be configured as: Visible only when s_status_group = OPEN_GROUP. Example: The 'Assign Team' button will be: Visible only when s_status_group = OPEN_GROUP and Role = Manager. Without the groups defined now, the Vienable configuration in Session 7 cannot be done. Part E — Updating the UI to Reflect Entity Configuration​ Now that d_complaints has Relations, Object Types, Status values, and an ID Series configured, the p_complaints page must be updated to expose and use these configurations. In this part you will: Add Relation-based TransNodes to p_complaints for d_complaint_item, d_complaint_voices, and d_complaints_attachment. Connect the s_complaint_item grid (already in the pa_comp_details tab from Session 2) to the d_complaint_item relation TransNode. Verify the complaint_id field auto-populates from the ID Series. Verify the s_status field on the search section and the detail form is bound and showing the correct status values. 📘 Why the UI Needs to Be Updated When you added Relations in Part A, the platform can now automatically fetch child records. But the Page Builder still needs to be told WHICH TransNode to use to access that relation data. A Relation-type TransNode in the Page Data Model references the relation name (pr_complaint_item) and automatically joins child records to the active parent complaint record. The complaint_id field in the form section can now be set to read-only since the ID Series will fill it — the user should not manually enter a complaint ID. E.1 — Add Relation TransNodes to the Page Data Model​ # Action Detail 1 Open Page Builder Navigate to Design Studio → Page Builder. Select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit icon to enable edit mode. 2 Select p_complaints Click p_complaints in the tree. Open the Page Data Model panel (right-side tab). 3 Review existing TransNodes You should see: search (Query), list (EntitySet / Transfer&Link from search), detail (Entity / Transfer&Link from list). These were created in Session 2. 4 Add complaint item TransNode Click the detail transnode → click + icon available next to r_complaint_item in unused properties. Fill: Path: complaint_items 6 Repeat Repeat Action 4 for relation voices, attachments 7 Save Click Save. E.2 — Wire the s_complaint_item Section to the Relation TransNode​ Need to create a s_complaint_item, s_complaint_voices, s_complaint_attachments section with screen_type as grid and bind with respective transnode. # Action Detail 1 Create s_complaint_item Right-click pa_complaint_details → new → section → right click section → rename : s_complaint_item 3 Mark type as section Add type = section for s_complaint_items layout 2 Open Detail panel Click s_complaint_item to open its Detail properties on the right. And fil title = items 3 Set TransNode path In the TransNode/Path field, set: complaint_items. This references the relation TransNode created in E.1 Step 4. 4 Add controls Right-click s_complaint_item → New → Controls. Add: item_id, product, issue_observed. Or drag from Page Data Model → d_complaint_item → Unused Properties. 5 Set screen type Confirm s_complaint_item screenType = grid. Set showTitle = true so the tab label 'Complaint Items' is visible. 6 Add Section Toolbar Right click on s_complaint_item → New → Toolbar Add and Delete buttons will be added to section if not enable showAdd and showDelete properties as true 7 Add Save Button Right click on the section toolbar → Action/Items → update text → add press event and select save from vh. 8 Add config Right click- s_complaint_item → new → config Add visibleRowCountMode = Fixed Repeat the same for s_complaint_voices and s_complaint_attachments as well with respective transnodes. E.4 — Verify s_status in Search and Detail Sections​ The s_status field is a system property. Now that Status values are configured in the BOL Editor (Part C), the status dropdown in the search section and detail form will automatically render the configured values (OPEN, INPROCESS, ON_HOLD, RESOLVED, CLOSED, REOPEN). # Action Detail 1 Click Show Full Preview Add the property in s_search and s_complaint_detail and In the Page Builder, click Show Full Preview to load live data. 2 Verify s_status in search bar In the search filter bar, click the Status dropdown. Verify the 6 status values appear: OPEN, INPROCESS, ON_HOLD, RESOLVED, CLOSED, REOPEN. 3 Click a complaint row Select any complaint record from the list. The detail area loads. 4 Verify complaint_id 1. For creating complaints with object_type enable showAddWithObjectType option for s_complaint_list section toolbar. 2. The complaint_id field should show the P-00001 or M-0001 format based on object_type (or different if the test record was created before the ID Series was set up — create a new record to confirm). 5 Verify Complaint Items tab Click the Complaint Items tab in the pa_comp_details area. If the selected complaint has items, they should appear in the grid. The tab was empty in Session 2 — it should now have a data source.

Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: Understand the three types of Value Helps (VH Config, VH Query, VH Transaction) and when to use each. Create a VH Config for priority (Low / Medium / High / Critical) and nature_of_complaint, complaint_type fields. Create VH Query types that fetch data from d_customers and d_resp_team entities as picker suggestions. Understand what a KloQuery is and how it differs from a Runtime Entity query. Create two Saved Queries for the complaint list: My Complaints (filtered by assigned_to = current user) and All Open Complaints (filtered by s_status = OPEN). Assign Value Helps to entity properties in the BOL Editor. Update the UI — wire VH pickers and query-driven TransNodes into the p_complaints search and detail sections. 📘 What This Session Builds On Session 3 configured Relations, Object Types, Status, and ID Series on d_complaints — the structural foundation. Session 4 makes the user experience intelligent: instead of typing raw IDs, users get dropdowns and pickers. priority, complaint_type, nature_of_complaint → VH Config (fixed, app-managed lists). customer_id, responsible_team → VH Query (dynamic, fetched from d_customers / d_resp_team). Saved Queries → drive the different list views per role (My Complaints for Employee, All Open for Manager). Part A — Understanding Value Helps​ A.1 — What Is a Value Help?​ A Value Help (VH) is a platform-level component that provides a controlled list of choices for an entity property. When a VH is assigned to a property, the corresponding input field in the UI automatically renders as a dropdown (ComboBox), auto-complete field, or picker dialog (F4) — without any additional coding. The VH also validates that the entered value exists in the list when 'Is Restricted' is enabled. 📘 Three VH Types in Klobase (VH User Guide — Section 1.1) VH Config: Values are maintained in the metadata (config) DB. App-managed, flavor-dependent. Can be overridden by child apps. Requires a build after creation/update. Use for fixed classification lists (priority, complaint_type, etc.). VH Query: Values are fetched from a transactional or modelled query at runtime. Use for dynamic master data pickers (customer_id, responsible_team). The query determines what data appears in the picker. VH Transaction (DEPRECATED): Older type. Internally still supported for legacy apps. New development should use VH Config or VH Query instead. VH Type Source Naming Use Case for This App VH Config Metadata / Config DB vhc_<name> priority, complaint_type, nature_of_complaint VH Query Transactional / Modelled Query vhq_<name> customer_id → d_customers, responsible_team → d_resp_team A.2 — Value Helps to Create in This Session​ VH ID Type Property to Assign Description vhc_priority VH Config priority Low / Medium / High / Very High vhc_complaint_type VH Config complaint_type Software vhc_nature_of_complaint VH Config nature_of_complaint Hardware : Battery not charging vhq_customer VH Query customer_id Fetches from d_customers — key: customer_id, display: customer_name vhq_resp_team VH Query responsible_team Fetches from d_resp_team — key: emp_id, display: name Part B — Creating VH Config Value Helps​ B.1 — What Is VH Config and When to Use It?​ VH Config stores its values in the metadata database — the same database that stores entity definitions, page structures, and app metadata. These values are part of the application definition itself, not the transaction data. Use VH Config for lists that are defined once by the developer and rarely change: priority levels, complaint categories, nature classifications. B.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating vhc_priority​ Follow these steps to create the priority VH Config. Repeat the process for vhc_complaint_type and vhc_nature. # Action Detail 1 Open Data Studio Navigate to Design Studio → Data Studio. Select your application customer_complaints_<prid> from the dropdown. 2 Click + → Value Help Select entity. Click the Add icon (+) in the toolbar. A menu appears — select Value Help. The Value Help creation dialog opens. 3 Fill VH ID and Type Value Help ID: vhc_priority 5 Fill VH detail fields Description: Priority levels for customer complaints 6 Add VH Config items Click the Add (+) icon in the VH Config Items section. Add Row 1: Key: LOW 7 Save Click Save. vhc_priority is saved. Note: a build is required for this to appear in the UI — proceed to create all VH Configs first, then the trainer will trigger the build. B.3 — Assign VH Config to Entity Properties​ After creating all three VH Configs, assign each to the corresponding property in d_complaints. This is done in the Properties tab of the entity. # Action Detail 1 Select d_complaints In the Data Studio tree, click d_complaints. 2 Go to Properties tab Click the Properties tab. Locate the priority property row. 3 Set Value Help for priority Click the Value Help column cell for the priority row. A value help picker opens — type vhc_priority and select it. The VH ID is now assigned to the property. 5 Repeat for complaint_type and nature_of_complaint Assign vhc_complaint_type to complaint_type property. Assign vhc_nature to nature_of_complaint property. 6 Save Click Save. All three properties now have VH Config assignments. ✔ VH Config Checkpoint vhc_priority created — 4 items: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL. vhc_complaint_type created — 5 items matching the Object Types from Session 3. vhc_nature created — 4 items: TECHNICAL, LOGISTICS, COMMERCIAL, GENERAL. All 3 VH Configs assigned to their respective d_complaints properties. Save confirmed for all. Part C — Creating VH Query Value Helps​ C.1 — What Is VH Query?​ A VH Query fetches its suggestion items from a live entity or modelled query at runtime. Unlike VH Config (which is static metadata), VH Query shows records that are currently in the transactional database. This is the right choice for master entity pickers — where the data comes from d_customers, d_resp_team, or any other entity that can be searched and selected. 📘 VH Query Fields (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 2.2.3 Value Help Detail) Entity/Query: The entity name or modelled query ID that returns the list of suggestions. Key Property: The property whose value gets STORED in the parent entity when the user selects an item. For d_customers → customer_id. Display Text: The property shown to the user in the dropdown/picker. For d_customers → customer_name. Desc Format: How the display appears. Example: :customer_id--:customer_name shows ID followed by Name. Icon: Optional — entity property that holds an icon URL to show alongside each suggestion item. C.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating vhq_customer​ # Action Detail 1 Click + → Value Help Select entity and In the Data Studio toolbar, click + → Value Help. Value Help ID: vhq_customer 2 Open vhq_customer Click vhq_customer in the tree. The Detail panel shows the VH Query configuration fields. 3 Set Entity/Query In the Entity/Query field, select d_customers. This means the VH will execute a runtime query against d_customers to fetch suggestion rows. 4 Set Key Property Key Property: customer_id. This is the value that gets written into d_complaints.customer_id when the user picks a customer. 5 Set Display Text Display Text: customer_name. This is what the user sees in the dropdown list. 6 Set Desc Format Desc Format: :customer_id--:customer_name. This renders as 'CUST-001 -- Acme Corp' in the picker field once a value is selected. 7 Save Click Save. vhq_customer is ready. Perform the same for vhq\_res\_team C.4 — Assign VH Query to Entity Properties​ # Action Detail 1 Select d_complaints → Properties tab Click on d_complaints in the tree and go to Properties. 2 Assign vhq_customer to customer_id Click the Value Help cell for customer_id. Select vhq_customer from the picker. Optionally mark Is Restricted = true to enforce that only valid customer records can be entered. 3 Assign vhq_resp_team to responsible_team Click the Value Help cell for responsible_team. Select vhq_resp_team. 4 Save Click Save. 💡 VH Type in the UI Control (KloControls 7.0 User Guide — KloInput) After assigning a VH to a property, the KloInput control in the UI renders differently based on the vhType setting in the Page Data Model or the control's properties panel. F4: Shows a full picker dialog when the user clicks the input — best for large datasets (d_customers with many records). ComboBox: Shows a dropdown list — best for small fixed lists (priority, complaint_type). AutoComplete: Shows suggestions as the user types — best for name-search scenarios. The platform automatically uses the appropriate type based on the VH type. You can override it in the Page Data Model or the control properties. Part D — Understanding and Creating KloQueries​ D.1 — What Is a KloQuery?​ A KloQuery is the Klobase equivalent of a SQL SELECT statement. It lets you define — within the Data Studio — exactly what records to fetch, from which entity, with which filters, joins, and sort order. Unlike a Runtime Entity Query (which simply fetches all records of an entity), a Modelled Query gives you full control over the WHERE clause, JOIN entities, and sort order — and is reusable across multiple pages. Query Type When to Use Runtime Query (Entity Query) Fetch all records of a single entity. No WHERE clause in the definition. Filters applied at runtime via the TransNode. Use for simple list screens. Modelled Query (Dynamic Query) Define custom WHERE conditions, joins, sort order in the BOL Editor. Reusable, entity-independent. Use for role-filtered lists (My Complaints), VH Queries backed by joins, aggregated results. Native Query (Advanced Query) Raw SQL. Database-specific. Use only for special cases not achievable with modelled queries. Avoid training. 📘 KloQuery Fields Reference (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.2) Return Entity: The entity whose properties appear in the result set. Query Type: Runtime Entities And Join: Add the root entity and any joined entities (LEFT JOIN, INNER JOIN, etc.). Select Properties: Choose which properties from the entities appear in the result. Parameters: Define input parameters the query accepts at runtime (e.g., user_id filter passed from the TransNode). Where: Define filter conditions: entity.property = :parameter or entity.property = 'fixed_value'. Sort Order: Set the default sorting column and direction (ASC / DESC). Naming convention: Query IDs must start with q_. All lowercase. D.2 — Queries to Create in This Session​ Query ID Type Purpose q_complaints Modelled Employee: shows only complaints assigned to the logged-in user D.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating q_my_complaints​ # Action Detail 1 Click + → Query Select d_complaints entity and click + → Query. Fill : q_complaints and click create then save. 2 Open q_complaints Click q_my_complaints in the tree. The Detail panel shows the query configuration tabs. 4 Select Properties tab Click the Select Properties tab. By default, all d_complaints properties are included. Remove any you do not need to reduce payload. Keep it all for now. 5 Add Parameter Click the Parameters tab. Click Add. Parameter ID: current_user 6 Add WHERE clause Click the Where tab. Click Add. Fill: Entity Property: d_complaints.assigned_to 7 Add Sort Order Click the Sort Order tab. Click Add. Field: d_complaints.created_on 8 Save Click Save. q_my_complaints is ready. Part E — Saved Queries​ E.1 — What Is a Saved Query?​ A Saved Query is a named combination of a base query and a specific set of pre-filled search parameters. Where a Modelled Query defines the structure, a Saved Query defines a pre-configured instance of that query — ready to execute with one click in the search bar. Saved Queries appear as quick-filter options in the search TransNode of the UI. 📘 Saved Query vs Modelled Query (Basic Training Guide — Section 2.1) Modelled Query: The definition — entity, properties, parameters, WHERE logic. Reusable structure. Saved Query: A named configuration of a modelled query with preset parameter values. Stored per entity. In the UI, a Saved Query appears as a quick-filter button or dropdown in the search bar section. Saved Queries are created from the Data Browser (Advanced Search), not directly in the query detail tab. Naming convention for Saved Query IDs: Begin with sq_ by convention. E.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Saved Query from Data Browser​ # Action Detail 1 Open Data Browser Select d_complaints in the Data Studio tree. Click the data browser in the toolbar. The Data Browser opens. 2 Open Advanced Search In the Data Browser toolbar, click the Advance Search button. A search configuration dialog opens. 3 Select Base Query In the Query field of the Advance click + 4 Set parameter values Select customer_id in the left input and like in the middle input. Enter: $SYSTEM.userID as the parameter value. This means the saved query will always use the logged-in user's ID at runtime. 5 Save as Saved Query Click the Save Query button (or the Save icon in the Advance Search toolbar). Enter Saved Query ID: sq_my_complaints 6 Verify Click search. The Data Browser should show only complaints where assigned_to matches the current user (or empty if no matches). The saved query is now available. Part F — Updating the UI to Use Value Helps and Queries​ With all Value Helps and Queries configured in the BOL Editor, the p_complaints page now needs to be updated to use them. In this part you will: Update the search TransNode to use q_complaints_list as its data source. Add the quick-filter Saved Query buttons (sq_my_complaints, sq_all_open) to the search section. Verify that priority, complaint_type, customer_id, and responsible_team fields in the form render as dropdowns/pickers automatically. Set the vhType on customer_id and responsible_team controls to F4 (full picker dialog). F.1 — Update the TransNode to Use q_complaints_list instead d_complaints​ Currently the search TransNode uses the default entity fetch. Switching it to q_complaints_list gives you control over sort order and allows future WHERE customisation. # Action Detail 1 Open Page Builder Navigate to Design Studio → Page Builder. Select your app. Click the Edit icon. 2 Select p_complaints → Page Data Model Click p_complaints in the tree. Open the Page Data Model panel (right-side tab). 3 Update the search TransNode Delete the existing transnode (search → list → detail) and create the same with q_complaints instead of d_complaints and verify bindings once more. 4 Save Click Save. F.2 — Verify VH Controls Render Correctly in Full Preview​ After the build is triggered by the trainer (required for VH Config changes), verify the following in Full Preview: # Action Detail 1 Click Show Full Preview Click Show Full Preview in the Page Builder toolbar. 2 Verify priority dropdown In the search filter bar, click the Priority field. It should render as a dropdown (ComboBox) showing: Low, Medium, High, . 3 Verify complaint_type dropdown Click the Complaint Type field in search. Should show: Product Issue, Billing Issue, Delivery Issue, Service Issue, General. 4 Verify customer_id picker Click a complaint row to load the details. In the detail form, click the customer_id (Employee ID) field. An F4 picker dialog should open listing all d_customers records with their names. 5 Verify responsible_team picker In the detail form, click the responsible_team field. The picker should show d_resp_team records (name + emp_id). 6 Test a selection Select a customer from the customer_id picker. Save the complaint. Verify the customer_id value is stored correctly (the KEY, not the display text) by checking the Data Browser. 💡 VH Type (F4 / ComboBox / AutoComplete) Override The Page Data Model assigns a default vhType to each property with a VH. You can override it per control in the Page Builder. To change vhType on a specific control: Click the control in the tree → Detail panel → find vhType property → change to F4, ComboBox, or AutoComplete. For customer_id and responsible_team: use F4 (full picker with search) since the lists may grow large. For priority, complaint_type, nature_of_complaint: ComboBox is ideal (small fixed list, no search needed). ✔ UI Wiring Checkpoint — Verify Before Session 4 Assignment search TransNode on p_complaints updated to q_complaints_list (Modelled Query). s_search section has 2 Saved Query quick-filters: 'My Complaints' and 'All Open'. Full Preview (post-build): priority dropdown shows Low/Medium/High/Critical. Full Preview: complaint_type dropdown shows 5 type options. Full Preview: customer_id field opens F4 picker with d_customers records. Full Preview: responsible_team field opens F4 picker with d_resp_team records. Full Preview: 'My Complaints' button filters list to current user's complaints.
