documents.t: A.1 — What Is the Menu Editor?​ The Menu Editor (also called Menu Builder per PROC-26419) is the tool you use to define the navigation structure visible to users in the hamburger menu of the application at runtime. Without a menu entry, users cannot navigate between screens — they would need to know URLs manually. Access path: Running app → Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → Menu Editor. A.2 — Menu Fields Reference​ Field Description Rules / Notes Menu ID Unique identifier for this menu item. ONLY alphanumeric + underscores. NO hyphens ( - ). NO spaces. Case-sensitive. Wrong: mn-complaints. Correct: mn_complaints. Target Page Page ID the menu item navigates to. Use the Value Help (VH) icon to pick from existing pages. Do NOT type the page ID manually. Menu Text Label shown to the user in the hamburger menu. Keep it short. Title case. Localisation supported. Page Parameters Optional JSON for navTo params (SS, QP, D, Mode). Leave blank for simple page nav. Not needed for the Complaints entry. Menu Icon SAP icon URI displayed alongside the text. Format: sap-icon://<icon-name>. Must be a valid SAP UI5 icon name. Example: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts. Sequence Sort order in the menu. Lower number = appears first. Use multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30) to leave room for future items. Roles Restrict visibility to specific application roles. Leave BLANK = visible to ALL roles. Fill role IDs (comma-separated) to restrict. Test Navigation Validates the menu item navigates correctly. Always click Test Navigation before saving — catches target page errors early. A.3 — BRD Menu Structure to Implement​ Menu Field Value Menu ID mn_complaints Target Page p_complaints (select from VH) Menu Text Complaints Menu Icon sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence 10 Roles Leave blank — visible to ALL roles (Employee, Manager, IT Team) Page Parameters Not required — leave blank A.4 — Step-by-Step: Creating the Application Menu​ 1 Open Menu Editor In the running application, open the hamburger menu (☰ top-left). Go to Dev Tools → Menu Editor. 2 Select the Application In the App dropdown at the top of the Menu Editor, select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏). The menu table becomes editable. 3 Add a Header Group Click Add (+) → Add Header. Fill in: Menu ID: hdr_main Menu Text: Main Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. (A Header groups child items visually in the menu.) 4 Add the Complaints Child Menu Item Select the hdr_main row in the table. Click Add (+) → Add Child. Fill in: Menu ID: mn_complaints Target Page: p_complaints (use VH picker) Menu Text: Complaints Menu Icon: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. 5 Test the Navigation Click Test Navigation on the mn_complaints row. p_complaints should open correctly. If a 'Page not found' error appears — check that the Target Page is exactly p_complaints (no typos). 6 Save Click the Save button (disk icon 💾). Wait for the busy dialog to close. A success toast confirms the menu is saved. 7 Verify with All Personas Log out and log in separately as emp_<prid>, mgr_<prid>, and it_<prid>. In each session, open the hamburger menu. The 'Complaints' item must be visible and navigate to p_complaints for ALL three test users. ⚠ Important Common Menu Editor Mistakes Hyphen in Menu ID: mn-complaints causes the item to save but NEVER appear in the app. Always use underscore: mn_complaints. Typing Target Page manually: Always use the VH picker. Manual typos cause silent navigation failures. Saving without testing: Always click 'Test Navigation' before saving. It catches missing pages early. Role restriction accident: If the menu item is set to a specific role, other personas cannot see it. Leave Roles blank for all-role visibility.

B.1 — What Is the HomePage Editor?​ The HomePage Editor configures which screen tiles appear on the application's built-in Home grid — accessible via the Home (🏠) icon. This is separate from the Landing Page (p_complaint_dashboard configured in Session 5). The Landing Page loads automatically on login. The Home grid gives users tile-based navigation to frequently used screens. 📘 Reference / Tip Three 'home' concepts — don't confuse them Landing Page (Session 5): Configured via Landing Page Settings. Auto-loads after login. Shows p_complaint_dashboard. HomePage Editor: Tile grid shown when user clicks the Home (🏠) icon. Configure p_complaints and p_complaint_dashboard tiles here. p_home_page (BRD): A screen defined in the BRD. Can be built as an additional home screen — not required for this session's delivery. B.2 — HomePage Editor Fields Reference​ Field Description HomePageID Unique ID for this tile. Convention: hp_<screen_short_name>. Screen The Page ID this tile navigates to. Use VH to select. Position Where the tile appears on the home grid. Use 'Body' for standard tiles. Sequence Order of the tile. Lower = appears first. Role Restrict tile visibility to specific roles. Leave blank = all roles. B.3 — Step-by-Step: Adding Tiles to HomePage Editor​ 1 Open HomePage Editor Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → HomePage Editor. Select customer_complaints_<prid> from the App dropdown. Click the Edit icon (✏). 2 Add the Dashboard Tile Click Add (+). HomePageID: hp_dashboard Screen: p_complaint_dashboard (select via VH) Position: Body Sequence: 5 Role: leave blank (all roles) Click Save (do NOT navigate away yet). 3 Add the Complaints Tile Click Add (+). HomePageID: hp_all_complaints Screen: p_complaints (select via VH) Position: Body Sequence: 10 Role: leave blank (all roles) Click Save. 4 Save All Click the Save icon (💾) in the toolbar. Wait for busy dialog to close. Success toast confirms. 5 Verify Log out. Log in as emp_<prid>. Click the Home (🏠) icon. Two tiles must appear: 'Dashboard' and 'Complaints'. Click each tile — verify it navigates to the correct screen. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>.

C.1 — App Status Values​ Every version of an application on the Procify platform has a Status that controls what operations are allowed on it. Understanding these statuses is essential before releasing or transporting. Status Meaning Can Develop? Can Transport? Can Create New Version? ACTIVE Current working version. All development happens here. ✅ Yes ❌ No ❌ No RELEASED Development complete and locked. Ready for transport. ❌ No ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (create from RELEASED) DEPRECATED Retired. Superseded by a newer version. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No DISCARDED Abandoned branch/version. Excluded from main path. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No ⚠ Important Critical Versioning Rules — memorise these before proceeding A NEW VERSION can only be created from a RELEASED version. A BRANCH can only be created from an ACTIVE version. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Merge the branch into a new version first, then transport. Once status is changed to RELEASED, no further development is possible on that version. Always build (Validate & Publish) BEFORE changing status to RELEASED. C.2 — Step-by-Step: Releasing the Application​ 1 Navigate to Account Console (also called Workspace Hub) Open the hamburger menu → Sys Admin → Account Console (or Workspace Hub). Alternatively: Hamburger menu → My Apps (if visible in your role). 2 Find Your Application In the Apps list, search for customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the App ID to open the application detail screen. 3 Open Edit Mode Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏) in the toolbar. The Status field becomes editable. 4 Change Status to RELEASED In the Status dropdown, select RELEASED. Read the confirmation message carefully — this action locks all development on this version. Click Save. The app status changes to RELEASED. The Edit icon in Data Studio and Page Builder will now be disabled for this version. 5 Verify In the App detail, the Status badge shows RELEASED. Open Data Studio → select customer_complaints_<prid> → click the Edit icon. You should see a message that the app is locked for editing.
documents.s: Part C — App Status Lifecycle & Versioning

documents.t: D.1 — Why Branch?​ A Branch creates a parallel ACTIVE copy of your application. Use it when you need to work on next-phase enhancements while the current version is being tested in QA. The branch is fully isolated — changes in the branch don't affect the main RELEASED version until you explicitly merge them. Scenario Use Branch? Bug fix on the current version in QA ❌ No — fix directly in main, create new minor version New feature development while current is in QA ✅ Yes — branch from current ACTIVE version Experimental UI changes for client review ✅ Yes — branch lets you show without committing to main D.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Branch​ 1 Go to Account Console → My Apps Locate customer_complaints_<prid>. The app must be in ACTIVE status to create a branch. 2 Click Branch In the app detail view, click the Branch button (visible only when status = ACTIVE). The platform creates a new Branch Flavor automatically. The branch version appears in the My Apps list with a branch indicator. 3 Assign Users to the Branch Click the branch version to open its detail. Go to the Roles & Users tab → click Edit. Assign ALL three test users and your developer account to their respective roles. ⚠ Users are NOT copied automatically from the parent — you must assign them manually in the branch. 4 Develop in the Branch Open Data Studio or Page Builder. In the App dropdown, select the BRANCH version (not the main version). Make your changes. Save and test independently. D.3 — Branch Merge Workflow (Summary)​ When the branch is ready to be merged back into the main release cycle: 1 Export Both ZIPs Account Console → Export section. Download ZIP of the main RELEASED version (Set 1) and the branch version (Set 2). 2 Open App Compare & Merge Account Console → App Compare & Merge. Upload Set 1 (main) as Left and Set 2 (branch) as Right. Click Compare. 3 Review the Differences The tool lists differences per component: entities, pages, queries, VH, menus, etc. For each difference, select which version to keep: Set 1 (main), Set 2 (branch), or a Custom combination. 4 Download Merged ZIP Once all decisions are made, click Download to export the merged ZIP. 5 Create New Version and Import In Account Console, create a new Major or Minor version from the current RELEASED main version. Import the merged ZIP into the new version. Run Update Schema, Full Build, and test before releasing. 📘 Reference / Tip Reference: App Branching & Merging User Guide — App_Branching___Merging-User_Guide.docx PROC-26419 note: 'Account Console' may be renamed 'Workspace Hub' in platform help content. Both names refer to the same tool.
documents.s: Part D — App Branching and Merging

documents.t: E.1 — Validate vs. Publish — What's the Difference?​ Action What It Does When to Use Validate Scans the application for errors WITHOUT building. Safe — nothing changes in the running app. Run first, every time. Fix all errors before triggering Publish. Publish Validates first, then builds the app if no blocking errors exist. Updates the running app. After Validate passes with 0 errors. Use Full Build for first publish or after VH Config changes. E.2 — Common Publish Blockers​ Blocker Cause Fix VH Config not visible in UI after Publish VH Config changes require a Full Build. Always select 'Full Build' for the first publish or after adding/editing VH Configs. TypeScript compilation error Syntax error in entity .ts or controller .ts file. Open VS Code → check terminal for tsc errors → fix, save, re-validate. Update Schema not run Entity properties added but schema not updated in DB. Data Studio → select entity → Update Schema → confirm success toast. Another build IN-QUEUE A previous build is already running. Click 'Proceed' to queue behind the current build. Do NOT cancel it. Missing app_util flavor Validate and Publish menu not visible. Ask trainer — app_util must be assigned to your developer account. E.3 — Step-by-Step: Validate and Publish​ 1 Open Validate and Publish Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → Validate and Publish. (If this menu item is missing, app_util flavor is not assigned to your account. Ask the trainer.) 2 Enter the Application In the App field, type customer_complaints_<prid> and press Enter. The application version details load. 3 Run Validate First Select Action: Validate. Click Submit. Wait for the validation report to generate. Download the XLSX report if errors are listed. Fix every ERROR before proceeding. Warnings can be reviewed but do not block the build. 4 Fix All Errors For each error in the report: - Missing Update Schema → Data Studio → Update Schema on the entity. - TypeScript error → VS Code → fix tsc error → save → re-validate. - Missing VH Build → select Full Build in the next step. Re-run Validate until the report shows 0 errors. 5 Run Publish Select Action: Publish. Build Type: Full Build (required for first publish and after any VH Config changes). Click Submit. The Publish Log shows the progression: IN-QUEUE → IN-PROCESS → PUBLISHED Do NOT navigate away while the build is running. 6 Verify the Published App Log out completely. Log back in. Open the hamburger menu → confirm 'Complaints' item is visible. Navigate to p_complaints → confirm live data loads. Verify: status badges render, VH dropdowns populate, all tabs in detail section work. 📘 Reference / Tip Publish Logs reference: Publish_Logs_Screen.docx — explains each status stage and error codes. Validate & Publish reference: Publish_or_Validate_Screen-7_0_App_utility__.docx

F.1 — How Transport Works​ Transport is a PULL mechanism: the TARGET system (QA) asks the SOURCE system (DEV) for the latest published version. You perform ALL transport steps while logged into the QA environment, not DEV. Stage What Happens Setup Transport creates entries in QA metadata tables for the application, groups, and flavors. Download Application ZIPs are pulled from DEV and extracted in the QA server's file system. Update Schema Database tables for all entities are created or altered in the QA database. Finalising Application is set to ACTIVE in QA so users can log in and access it. ⚠ Important Transport Pre-requisites — verify ALL before starting 1. The application must be in RELEASED status on the DEV system. 2. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Create a new version, merge, then transport. 3. The QA server's config.json must have mm_klo_online_server pointing to the DEV landscape URL. 4. A host file entry for the DEV system must exist on the QA server. 5. The transport_1 app must be assigned to the developer account on the QA system. If any pre-requisite is missing, the transport will fail at Setup or Download stage. Ask the trainer to verify the QA environment config before proceeding. F.2 — Step-by-Step: Transporting to QA​ 1 Log in to the QA System Open the QA environment URL in a browser (trainer provides the URL). Log in with your developer credentials. ⚠ ALL remaining steps are done on QA, not on DEV. 2 Navigate to App Transport Hamburger menu (☰) → Sys Admin → App Transport. The App Transport screen lists all available applications from the connected DEV system. 3 Find Your Application In the list, locate customer_complaints_<prid>. If not visible, toggle the 'Show All' button to see all available apps (not just those with pending updates). 4 Click the App Row Click on customer_complaints_<prid>. A detail panel opens showing available versions from DEV and any already-installed versions in QA. 5 Install As Writable Click the available version update. A dialog appears with two options: As Readable — locked, cannot edit in QA. As Writable — editable, allows continued development in QA. Click 'As Writable' (recommended for training so you can fix issues in QA if needed). 6 Accept Conditions and Proceed A mandatory conditions dialog appears. For each mandatory item (⚠ icon), tick the acceptance checkbox. If prompted about shared flavor movement (on QA/PROD systems), click Proceed. Click Proceed to start the transport. 7 Monitor Transport Stages The screen shows progress through: Setup → Download → Update Schema → Finalising. Wait for each stage to complete. The overall status changes to ACTIVE when done. 8 Assign Users in QA After transport, the app is ACTIVE in QA but has NO users assigned. Go to Account Console → My Apps → customer_complaints_<prid>. Go to Roles & Users tab → assign: emp_<prid> → Employee role mgr_<prid> → Manager role it_<prid> → ResponsibleTeam role Your developer account → Manager role 9 Verify in QA Log out of the QA developer session. Log in as emp_<prid> in QA. Verify: hamburger menu shows 'Complaints', p_complaints loads, all VH dropdowns work. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>. 📘 Reference / Tip Transport User Guide: Transport-_User_Guide.docx The Transport tool supports DEV → QA, QA → PROD, and DEV → DEV movement. Script Master (second tab in Transport screen) shows automated scripts maintained for the system — ask trainer if any scripts need to be run after transport.

documents.t: This smoke test must be completed AFTER publish. It verifies every major feature built across all 8 sessions works correctly in the published application. Run it on DEV first, then repeat on QA after transport. # Persona Action Expected Result 1 EMPLOYEE (emp_<prid>) Login → Menu → Complaints. Click Add (with Object Type = PROCIFY). Fill complaint_desc (10+ chars), priority = HIGH, select customer from picker. Click Save. complaint_id = P-000XX auto-generated. s_status = OPEN. assigned_to = emp_<prid>. Record appears in list. 2 EMPLOYEE Open the new complaint → Edit → Clear complaint_desc → Save. V001 error blocks save: 'Complaint description must be at least 10 characters'. 3 EMPLOYEE Edit → priority dropdown. ComboBox shows Low / Medium / High / Critical (from vhc_priority). 4 EMPLOYEE Edit → customer_id field. F4 picker opens showing d_customers records. 5 MANAGER (mgr_<prid>) Login → open the OPEN complaint → Edit → set responsible_team from picker → Save. responsible_team field is editable for Manager. Record saves. Status remains OPEN. 6 IT TEAM (it_<prid>) Login → open assigned complaint → Edit → s_status = INPROCESS → Save. Status badge changes to INPROCESS (orange colour). Edit button remains visible. 7 EMPLOYEE Open INPROCESS complaint → Edit → try s_status = CLOSED → Save. V005 error: 'Employees cannot close a complaint'. 8 MANAGER Open INPROCESS complaint → Edit → s_status = CLOSED → closed_on = today → Save. Status badge changes to CLOSED (grey). Edit button disappears (COMPLETED Vienable). actual_tat computed in Data Browser. 9 ALL ROLES Navigate to Home (🏠). Two tiles visible: Dashboard and Complaints. Each tile navigates correctly. 10 ALL ROLES Preview In → Phone (Page Builder). Grid in s_complaints shows only 3 columns (ticket_id, priority, s_status) on phone view.

Concept What It Does Where to Configure Menu Editor (Menu Builder) Defines hamburger menu structure. Roles blank = all users. NO hyphens in Menu ID. Dev Tools → Menu Editor → select app → Edit Header + Child Item Header groups child menu items visually. Children point to actual screens. Menu Editor → Add → Add Header, then Add → Add Child sap-icon:// SAP UI5 icon URI format used in menu and controls. Menu Editor → Menu Icon field HomePage Editor Adds tiles to the Home (🏠) grid. Separate from Landing Page. Dev Tools → HomePage Editor Landing Page Settings Sets auto-load screen after login. Configured in Session 5. Dev Tools → Landing Page Settings App Status: RELEASED Locks development. Enables transport. New version must be created from RELEASED. Account Console → My Apps → Status field Branch Parallel ACTIVE copy for next-phase development. Not transportable directly. Account Console → My Apps → Branch button (ACTIVE only) App Compare & Merge Compares two ZIP exports; per-component merge decisions; produces merged ZIP. Account Console → App Compare & Merge Validate Checks for errors. Safe — nothing deployed. Download XLSX report. Dev Tools → Validate and Publish → Action: Validate Publish (Full Build) Validates then builds. VH Config changes REQUIRE Full Build. Dev Tools → Validate and Publish → Action: Publish → Full Build Transport (Pull) QA pulls RELEASED app from DEV. Requires config, host, transport_1 app. QA system → Sys Admin → App Transport

Log on to the test system. (Get all the credentials from the Admin Team) User: Use your User ID (PRID) Password: Use your password. The Data Studio app will be assigned to you.

Data that are stored in the database are in table format. Data Studio is used to create tables for our database. In BOL, all entities and queries act as attributes of the table. 1.0.1 The Editor is divided into two major sections: Tree Detail
The app or Flavor selection drop-down contains a list of apps that have been assigned to the user. By using the drop down users can select the app on which users are going to work on.
Once the app is selected, it will list down all the entities present inside the selected app. To select any specific entity, click on that entity.
You can search for any entity by filling in the entity name in the search field provided in the entity list section.

Data Studio supports two types of modes, Normal mode and Expert mode. Normal Mode - It supports all the basic functionalities like Entity, Query, and Value Help creation along with app settings. Expert Mode - It supports all the functionalities from the normal mode along with add-on features like Status Config, config properties for object type, and entity indexes. Note: One can switch between the two modes at any point in time.
Create button lists down various options for table creation. Create Menu supports the below actions: Entity Entity From Template Query Value Help

By default, the editor will be in non-editable mode. Clicking on the edit button will make the data editable. Once the edit mode is enabled, it will update the list of available options in the toolbar. The mode gets changed to editable and the save option will be enabled. The below icon shows the save icon which will be used for committing the changes to the DB.

Once the entity is in editable mode, it lists down the list of available options as shown in the below image. 1.7.1. Update Schema​ Once all the metadata regarding the entity is provided and saved, the update schema is used to convert the entity into an actual database table. 1.7.2. Delete​ This option will be used for deleting any item selected in the left tree. Using this option, any item like entity/query or value help can be deleted. 1.7.3. Validate​ The validate option verifies whether the metadata maintained for the entity is correct or not. 1.7.4. Read Only​ The read-only and cancel options are only visible in editable mode. On the click of the read-only icon, the editor becomes non-editable. 1.7.5. MetaData File​ This comprises the metadata file that you want to upload from your local system to the Data Studio. 1.7.6 Test​ Test allows checking the CRUD operation on the created/selected which stands for create, read, update, and delete. These are four basic functions executed in relational database applications. 1.7.7. Import from SAP​ This option imports the selected entity & its properties from SAP tables. Developers can import an entity -> verify their changes -> and then click "Save" to commit their changes. Pre-requisite: In config.json, under "mm_klobroker_ext" array, an object needs to be maintained having details as follow, mentioning the connection between your flavor in platform and the respective SAP system: The flavor should have some entities already maintained in SAP-side which will be used to import. Steps: Navigate to "Design Studio" -> "Data Studio" Screen and select your flavor. The flavor needs to be configured on the SAP side. The flavor_name and major_version should be the same. The minor version and patch version can be different from each other. Create a new entity and do not add any properties yet. Otherwise, use an existing entity having some existing properties. And then click the "Import from SAP" button. If the entity is maintained in the SAP-side, then it will show an error dialog. Else, the import process will start. Validation: During the process, if any error comes it will throw the error dialog. And in case any validation fails e.g., propertyid values are having reserved keywords then it will show that respective dialog also - same validation as available we developer normally create properties from the screen. List of reserved keywords: PROC-27544: List of Reserved Keywords in Data Studio Application. Once the import process starts, at the end step, it will ask the developer to skip any specific properties by selecting the checkbox and clicking the "Skip" button or click "Sync All" to accept all data from the payload. Important: Import from SAP on Existing Entity After import is done, developers can save more properties and save it. Note: SAP Import process only imports the entity and properties. After import, the developer needs to click the Save button to commit all changes. 1.7.7.1. Import from SAP on Existing Entity Data​ While doing import again on an existing entity having existing properties, it will ask the developer regarding the existing properties whether to keep those properties or delete them. For example, here my_key_1 is a property not present in the sap table and is an existing property in the Procify-side table. So, here, if the developer will mark the checkbox of it and click "Skip", then it will not delete that property. If the developer clicks "Sync All", then it will delete the existing properties and import only SAP-side, non-skipped properties. 1.7.8. Import from SAP Child​ This option imports the children entity(s) from an existing parent entity from SAP tables. Does not include relations. Developers can import an entity -> verify their changes -> and then click "Save" to commit their changes. Pre-requisite is the same as mentioned in the Import from SAP section. Steps: Validation: If a developer has created a parent entity and triggered "Import from SAP Child" before saving the parent entity, then it will throw a validation error. So, it is needed to create & save its parent entity first, before importing its respective children entities. If the parent entity is maintained in the SAP-side, then it will show an error dialog. Else, the import process will start. From Data Studio, select the flavor -> click the parent entity -> click edit button -> click "Import from SAP Child" button. Validation: During the process, if any error comes it will throw the error dialog. And in case any validation fails e.g., propertyid values are having reserved keywords then it will show that respective dialog also - same validation as available we developer normally create properties from the screen. List of reserved keywords: PROC-27544: List of Reserved Keywords in Data Studio Application. Once the import process starts, at the end step, it will ask the developer to skip any specific properties by selecting the checkbox and clicking the "Skip" button or click "Sync All" to accept all data from the payload. Important: Import from SAP Child on Existing Entity Important: Before Save, developers need to maintain the Primary Keys in all of the imported children entities. Otherwise, it will throw a validation error before clicking Save. After maintaining the Primary Keys in all imported children entities, it will allow the developers to save the changes. Important: As relations are not maintained via the import process, after save, developers need to maintain the relations manually from the Data Studio tool. a. Parent to Child Primary Relation: > b. Child to Grandchild Primary Relation: Once the relations are maintained, the developers can start using the entity's data browser or from screen for CRUD operations. 1.7.8.1. Import from SAP Child on Existing Entity Data​ Mentioned in 1.7.7.1 .
Data Studio is divided into two major sections, which are listed below: Tree Detail

The tree present in the left section lists all the entities present in the selected app. 2.1.1. Expand All​ Expand All option is to expand all the collapsed sections (entity, query, value help). 2.1.2 Collapse All​ Collapse all option is to collapse all the expanded sections (entity, query, value help)

This section contains all the details related to the selected entity/query or value help like properties, relations, object type, status, queries, and many more. 2.2.1 Entity Detail​ On selection of any entity in the tree, it will display all available options in the detail section. The description of each tab is given below: 2.2.1.1. Detail​ This section contains all the basic information about the entity. It contains fields like Root Entity name, App Mode, Entity Icon, Entity Name, Metadata type, and also a few buttons to enable or disable CRUD over the entity. The description of each field is provided below: BO/Root Entity :​ BO stands for Business Object. Root Entity means that if any entity is a root entity then it will have the same name as the BO and it will be the parent entity. App Mode :​ App mode refers to the network mode of the entity/query. It supports network modes such as those specified below: Offline :​ Offline network mode refers to the capability to run the program with weak or infrequent network availability. The application stores the relevant data locally and updates the local cache and server data as and when it finds connectivity. Browsers and installed mobile apps (client) both are capable of offline operations. In offline mode, the values are maintained/fetched from the web SQL. Online :​ Online network mode refers to the capability of running the program in a browser or installed mobile app (client) to communicate with the server for day-to-day needs. Network connectivity from client to server is a must. All the changes on the browser or device app will be collected and sent to the server for validating and saving. In the online mode, the values are maintained/fetched from the transactional database. SAP Online :​ This refers to the capability of all the transactions that go to SAP via the gateway server. In SAP online mode the values are maintained/fetched from the SAP server. SAP Preferred Online :​ Any transaction that takes place between your application goes through SAP to your web SQL. Entity Icon :​ This will associate the specified icon with the entity. Entity Name :​ Entity name refers to the actual name/id of the entity. Metadata type:​ Runtime entity: This is the default type of entity, where the table persists in the DB (unlike Transient Entities). The table is created in the Trans DB and CRUD operations can be performed on it. Config entity: This is the type of entity, where the table persists but only in meta DB. This is usually used to store data for status and role fields. Transient Entities​ A transient entity is a non-persistent entity---meaning it does not store data in the database. It is primarily used for runtime calculations, data aggregation, or displaying derived data in the UI. These entities are ideal when you need to display or process combined data from multiple sources without storing it permanently. Use Case Example: Suppose you have two entities and want to display certain fields from each, but do not wish to persist the combined data. In this case: Create a transient entity that includes only the required properties. Write custom logic to query both source entities. Populate the transient entity with the result. Display this transient data on the screen with full support for UI features like Sort, Filter, and Fuzzy Search. Users can also fetch data from external sources, populate the transient entity, and leverage built-in platform features such as:Sort, Filter, Fuzzy search, Excel download,Pivot view (report/chart generation). NOTE: Data Must Be Fully Loaded:The transient entity's query must execute with loadAll: true. Unique Primary Key: Ensure that the transient entity has a unique primary key to enable proper identification and UI support. Custom Data Handling Logic: You must define how and from where the data is fetched, processed, and whether or not it should be saved back to a persistent entity. Persists On :​ Persists On consists of three options which are explained below: null -​ Entities will be created based on the app's network mode. Root :​ Root key​ All primary properties of a Business Object (BO) will be designated as Root keys in its child entities. Is Unique Key:​ A unique key can be assigned to any property, aside from the primary key. When a child entity is created, all the root and parent keys are automatically marked as unique, and an index is generated for them. Any regular property can be designated as a unique key. **Use Case of Unique Key: **Consider a student table that includes columns for registration number (reg_no), student name (student_name), and date of birth (date_of_birth), with multiple records where the reg_no is the primary key. reg_no(Primary) student_name date_of_birth 1001 Ankit 21/04/2001 1002 Abhijith 22/08/2005 1003 Amit 12/02/2004 1004 Prem 08/05/2000 ** **Consider adding a new column, "aadhar_no," to store the Aadhaar numbers of all the students. Since each Aadhaar number should be unique, we want to ensure the database doesn't allow duplicate entries. The only option available is to mark "aadhar_no" as a primary key, but this would prevent the user from making any updates to the existing data. To solve this, the concept of a unique key is introduced. By marking the "aadhar_no" as a unique key, we ensure that duplicate values can't be stored in the column while still allowing null values. This allows us to modify the data in the table without enforcing a primary key constraint. reg_no(Primary) student_name aadhar_no(unique) date_of_birth 1001 Ankit 21/04/2001 1002 Abhijith 22071 22/08/2005 1003 Amit 12/02/2004 1004 Prem 08/05/2000 When a property is marked as unique, it offers the following benefits: It prevents the storage of duplicate data, regardless of case (case-insensitive). It allows null values to be stored in the column. When creating a child entity, it is mandatory to mark a property as unique to support the "one parent, multiple children" concept. This is because the parent key, which is unique, will be fetched from the parent entity and referenced in the child. If someone tries to add another child with the same parent data, a unique key violation will occur. To resolve this, an additional unique key must be defined in the child entity that is independent of the parent entity. When a unique key is defined in a child entity that has a primary relationship with a parent entity, uniqueness is enforced as a composite constraint comprising the parent key and the child unique key (i.e., parent_key + unique_key). Transient Property:​ An entity property can be made transient by setting the type of property to "Transient Field" so that within that entity property's value is not stored in the database. It exists only at runtime and is never persisted in or retrieved from the database. Use Cases: **Accessing Properties of Relational Entities ** Transient fields can be used to display values from related entities without actually adding them as properties/database table columns. For example, if an entity is related to another entity(e.g., User → Department), a transient field like departmentName can fetch and show department.name without requiring an actual field in the database. **Custom Getter/Setter Logic **Standard transient property getters and setters can be used for dynamically calculating values, formatting data before sending it in a response, or temporarily accepting input and storing it without saving it to the database. In this example, d_customer is the entity, and fullName is a transient property. The fullName property is computed from the underlying firstName and lastName fields. The getter and setter for fullName should be written directly inside the entity file /src/<app folder>/entity/d_customer.ts Eg: get fullName(): string { return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`; } set fullName(name: string) { const [firstName, lastName] = name.split(' '); this.firstName = firstName; this.lastName = lastName; } Note : In case a user wants to change the property type of any property, they have to re-add the same property in their screen metadata using UI Editor (wherever applicable) from their transnode for reflecting the changes. Entity Index​ The Entity index tab is used to retrieve data from a database very fast. When you are creating indexing, It will create an index in your database along with the properties you have added. Next time when you search those properties, It will directly fetch that index from the database and give you the data. An index on a table works like an index in a book (that's where the name came from): Let's say you have a book about databases and want to find some information about storage. Without an index (assuming no other aid, such as a table of contents) you'd have to go through the pages one by one until you found the topic (that's a full table scan). On the other hand, an index has a list of keywords, so you'd consult the index and see that storage is mentioned on pages 113-120,231 and 354. Then you could flip to those pages directly, without searching (that's a search with an index, somewhat faster). Entity Index creation: Step 1: Go to the Entity Index tab and click on the add icon(+) Entity index consists of a few fields which are mentioned below: ID: The entity index ID is used to identify the specific entity index. Description: A short description of the entity index. Properties: Properties for your indexing. These properties data will be retrieved very fast. Client/Server: Entity indexing will call on which side, server-side, client-side or both. Step 2: Fill in the detail section as per your requirement. Step 3: Click on the save button. NOTE: Indices will be created based on the Client/Server mentioned. Server Only - Creates index only in server DB Client Only - Creates only in client/local DB Both - Creates on both server and client Deletion of Entity Indexes is supported at both entity level and flavor level update schema , but some points have to be kept under consideration. In a parent-child scenario, if an index is deleted from the parent but still exists in the child, triggering an update schema on the child entity will cause the index to be added back. To avoid inconsistencies, an index must be deleted from both the parent and child entities. 2.2.1.8. Debugging a Legacy to Klarion Server Callback on a Private Node:​ A Legacy to Klarion Server (E2K_MSG) rule runs when a legacy system, such as SAP, sends a message to the Klarion application. These messages are processed on the server nodes, so the rule can't normally be debugged from a private node. To debug such a rule, the node ID of the private node should be sent in the message header. The message is then processed on that private node, where breakpoints can be used like for any other rule. Steps: Start the private node and note its node ID. Send the message with the header nodeid set to the node ID of the private node. The private node picks up the message and runs the Legacy to Klarion Server (E2K_MSG) rule. Debug the rule from the debugger attached to the private node. NOTE: If the header is not sent, the message is processed on the server nodes as usual. 2.2.2. In the UI Editor, Page Data Model will be created from the Transient Entity rather than the return entity. The Transient Entity will include all the properties from the SELECT clause, ensuring that all values are properly displayed on the screen. Differences Between Aggregate and Native Aggregate Queries Aggregate query automatically generates a transient entity containing all properties used in the SELECT clause. If no SELECT clause is modeled, the return entity is used instead. Properties added automatically by the framework to the transient entity cannot be deleted. However, users can add their own properties to the transient entity for additional calculations, display purposes, or other operations. Native aggregate queries require the user to explicitly create a transient entity and assign it to the "Transient Entity" in the detail tab of the query. All aliases must be included as properties; if no alias is provided, the property name from the Entity should be included in the query. Note: For native aggregate queries, if a transient entity is not specified manually, it will be defaulted to the return entity. DB Selection:​ We have two DB instances, one is Reader and another is Writer, where Writer is RunTimeMain and Reader is RunTimeSecondary. We can shift the load of a particular query to the Reader instance by maintaining the proper DB Selection. By default it runs on RunTimeMain. In case of RunTimeSecondary, if we are updating some property of the entityset it will persist via RunTimeMain. Master data Transactional data SAVED_QUERY​ For the VH type Saved Query, first the user has to create a value help of type "QUERY" and then select in the parameter field a Saved Query ID, which will change the value help definition to "SAVED_QUERY" and will return a set of values and will be used as suggestion items. NOTE: Saved Query can be created from advance search in Data Browser. Entity authorization is automatically applied to the queries assigned to VH. Select the Object Type Value Help as Query. Select any existing Saved Query ID from the value help. Key Property & Display Text: If the provided saved query is created for an entity then it will contain the list of properties of that Entity. If the provided saved query is created for a query then it will contain the list of properties of the Return Entity of that Query. Dependents : If the provided saved query is created for an entity then it will contain the list of properties of that Entity. If the provided saved query is created for a query then it will contain the list of properties of the Return Entity of that Query. Icon: Entity property of return entity where SAPUI5 icon URL or image path is stored. VH_TRANSACTION​ VH Transaction is a common ValueHelp functionality provided by KloBase which can fulfil most of the basic requirements in the application. Here you can maintain the suggestion values for multiple ValueHelps. This is part of the transaction database. Which is also synced in the device at the time of initial sync and values are fetched from the same. No need to create any query. Icon:​ It is used in case we want to add an icon for any of the value help. Entity/Query:​ This will display the entity/query name associated with this value help. Desc Format:​ Desc format of a value help defines how the value help should be formatted and displayed. For Example: Desc Format = :id--:text Here ID and text should be replaced with entity property ID Key: The key is the property of the entity and needs to be selected from the drop-down. Display Text:​ Display text is also an entity property that needs to be selected from the dropdown.
This topic will guide you through the different object creations such as entity, query, and value help.

The data object in KloBase is known as Entity. An entity has one or more named properties, each of which can have one or more values. Each entity in the KloBase Datastore has a key that uniquely identifies it. In simple words, an Entity is a database table. Business Object (BO)​ Business Object (BO) is a logical unit used in a business. It is made up of one or multiple entities. BO is a hierarchical tree of entities. BO has only one root entity (top-level). The rest of the entities (child entities) are aggregated into root entities to construct the entity tree. The root entity represents the BO, root entity name becomes the BO name. Root entity also takes full responsibility as BO apart from its entity responsibility. Bo hierarchy​ d_order (root entity/BO) d_order_item (child entity) d_order_conditions (child entity) Create New Entity​ Step 1: Select the required App Once the Data Studio is loaded, select the app under which you want to create the new entity. Step 2: Select the Entity under the Create option Select the Add icon(+) option from the menu and click on Entity. Step 3: Fill in the details and create Fill in the entity name in the input field and click on the Create button. After following the above steps, it will navigate to the entity dashboard as shown below: Refer to the Detail Section for more information about the field shown here. Create New Entity from Excel:​ Note: Create an entity first and cancel for adding the first property popup Create a excel sheet like the below format: Add Status and Role sheet if applicable in the below format: Now click on the Data File and choose this file to upload and create properties and configs Creating Entity Property​ Step 1: Click on the add button in the properties tab Click on the properties tab and click on the Add (+) icon. Step 2: Select the required Qualifier It will open the qualifier menu, which gives the option to select the required qualifier for the property. Step 3: Fill the information in the field Fill in the required data such as entity property ID, key attributes, value help, and default value. For more information on each of the fields click here. Toggle the required icons as per the requirement such as primary key or mandatory field. Step 4: Save the entire process Once done with the entity and property creation, save the data. This action will push all the data into the database. Click on the save button in the toolbar. Once save is successful, the fields will become non-editable and in the toolbar, the edit icon will start appearing. Creating ID Series​ To navigate to the id-series section follow the below steps: Step 1: Go to Entity Properties Navigate to the properties tab after selecting the entity from the entity tree. Step 2: Click on the arrow to go to the main page Click on the right directional arrow, this will open the main dialog which will give access to ID series creation. Step 3: Add a new Entity Click on the Add icon to add a new entry in the id series section. Step 4: Fill in the details of your ID Series Fill in all the required details, close the dialog, and click on save. A new set of ID series has been created for the selected property. For more details about each of the fields continue reading below: ID: This field accepts the unique id of the id series as input. For naming convention click here. Object Type: If the order instance in question belongs to B1 and object type 1 then the order_b1_ot1_series definition will be picked for processing. If the order instance in question belongs to B1 and object type 2 then the order_b1_series definition will be picked for processing. If the order instance in question belongs to B2 and object type 3 then the order_base_series definition will be picked for processing. Type: Out of the listed options, the three that are widely used are explained below: GUID - Returns 32 char UUID as key. Autonumber - Returns incremental number for the allocated chunk. The auto number section. None - No number is assigned to the developer to fill the number. Generally used during override in tuner to remove the ID series. From: This takes the starting number/id series from where it will start generating numbers. Prefix: Prefix value for generating id series as a pattern. Suffix: Suffix value for generating id series as a pattern. Chunk Offline: Chunk offline is the number of entries you can create in your entity when network mode is offline. Everytime a new chunk is assigned to the user whenever he/she does an application registration. Chunk Size: Default 100 can be set to the desired number. Increment: It will accept the number by which the auto-generated number will be getting incremented. For example - From = 100, Increment = 1 So the next auto-generated number will be as follows: 101,102,103,104... Scope: The default is global, only one auto number is used for all the tenant and offline endpoint intervals. Pattern: Using the pattern option, we can generate the id series as a pattern, or by concatenating some string in the auto-generated number. For example - if we need a series like ORDER_ID-1103 Then we have to maintain the prefix in the pattern as ORDER_ID and the framework will automatically concat the auto-generated number with the entered string. Description: A short description explaining the use case/purpose of the id-series. Create Relations​ Step 1: Go To the Relations Tab Click on the Relations Tab. Step 2: Add a New Relation Now click on the add button to create a new relation and click on the key icon for primary relation or select the other icon for aggregate relation and fill in the other mandatory fields. Then click on the mapping icon. Step 3: Add source property information Add source property for the selected entity, mapping type, and target property for the chosen return entity after clicking on the add icon. Now save the relation. Create Object Type and Object Group​ Step 1: Go to the Object Type Tab Click on the Object Type Tab. Step 2: Add new Object Type Click on the add button to create a new object type. Fill in the object type. For more details on object type and object group, click here. Step 3: Click on the dialog icon Now click on the icon beside the object group value help to open the object group dialog. Step 4: Add Object Group In the object group dialog click on add and provide object group and description. Step 5: Now click on the cancel button on the top right. Step 6: Select Object Group Click on the icon present in the input field of Object Group and select the required object group. Click on Save to persist all the changes. Create Object Group Config​ Step 1: object Type Field Click on the object type tab Step 2: Click on the Add icon Click on the second section to add an icon. Select object Type, role ID and rollup status based on your requirement. Note: Click on save to save all the changes Create Status and Status Group​ Step 1: Status field Click on the Status Tab Step 2: Add Status Click on the add icon(+) to create a new status and fill in the mandatory fields. Now click on the save icon to save the particular mapping for the status. Create Entity Index​ Step 1: Entity Index field Click on the Entity Index Tab. Step 2: Add Entity Index Click on the add icon to create a new entity index and fill in the mandatory fields. Now click on the save icon to save the particular entity index data. Update Schema​ Once you are done with the entity and property creation, you can proceed with the updated schema. This will create the actual table in the database along with all the attributes. To perform an update schema, click on update schema. It will give a toast message like Updating Schema Done Successfully. After this step, our entity is ready for storing transactional data which will be used on the screen side or elsewhere. Now we have to store some data in the entity. It can be done using the Test option given in the toolbar. Incompatible changes​ If a property's type or attributes (e.g. precision, length) were changed in the metadata since the table was last created, clicking Update Schema may show a confirmation dialog listing the incompatible changes, for example: Some incompatible changes were found. Please press OK if you want to make the changes forcefully. NOTE: This will change / truncate the data in the table. followed by one line per affected property, e.g. Incompatible changes found (DEC:-decimal -> DEC:-decimal) in property:<property_name> in entity:<entity_name> in flavor:<flavor_name>. This means the metadata definition and the physical database column are out of sync --- usually because a prior property change (e.g. a precision or type change) was saved in metadata but Update Schema was not confirmed at that time. Clicking OK applies the change to the table forcefully. Existing data in the affected column(s) may be truncated or altered --- for example, reducing decimal precision will truncate any stored values beyond the new precision. Confirm this is acceptable, or back up/migrate the affected data first, before proceeding. Clicking Cancel leaves the table unchanged. The metadata will continue to report the new definition (e.g. the new precision) even though the underlying table still uses the old one --- this mismatch is silent and will resurface anywhere the discrepancy matters (e.g. UI display of decimal precision) until Update Schema is confirmed. Recommendation: Always confirm Update Schema in the same session as a property type/precision change, so metadata and the physical schema never drift apart. Data Browser​ The test is used for create, read, update, and delete. These are four basic functions executed in relational database applications. Clicking on TEST will take you to the Result table that has been created with all the entity properties and their functionalities. Advance Search​ In data browser dialog "Advance Search" option is there which is helpful in searching the required data from the list of entries made in the entity. Step 1: Click on advance search which will open a dialog. Click the add button to add an entry. Step 2: Fill the property id along with the operator and the value to be searched. Step 3: Use appropriate operators depending on the requirement. For ex: If data needs to be searched for any field which has multiple value then use "IN" operator. Note: If search parameters are needed to be saved then click on save button and provide an id. Delete ID Series​ To delete the ID series, follow the below steps: Step 1: Open the Data Studio and select the entity in which you want to delete the id series. Step 2: Click on the right directional arrow and open the dialog that lists down all the id series. Step 3: Select the ID series which you want to delete. Step 4: Click on the delete button. Step 5: Close the dialog and click on save. Delete Entity Property​ For deleting entity property, follow the below steps: Step 1: Open the Data Studio and select the entity in which you want to delete the property. Step 2: Click on the Properties tab and select the properties which you want to delete. Step 3: Click on the Delete button shown in the properties tab toolbar. Step 4: Click on the Save button. Delete an Entity​ For deleting an entity, follow these steps: Step 1: Open the Data Studio and select the app in which you want to delete the entity. Step 2: Select the entity from the left tree which you want to delete. You can select the entity by clicking on the entity name in the tree. Once an entity is selected, it will enable the detail section. Step 3: Click on the Edit icon in the editor toolbar if the editor is not in editable mode, then click the delete icon. Select OK in the confirmation dialog. Step 4: Click on the Save icon to save the changes and commit it to the DB.

kloQuery is a metamodel for fetching the data from the data store, like SQL in RDBMS. For example, the entity (table) name "d_order" has multiple columns including "s_status". To fetch all the records for open order in RDBMS need SQL as "Select ord_id, qty, ord_date from d_order WHERE d_order.status = 'open' Orderby ord_date ASC" and execute to get the desired result. kloQuery behaves similarly with a few value-added services, it gives the ability to fetch the data seamlessly for both offline and online applications. Abstracts out multiple syntaxes of Odata, SQL, JSON, etc. so that programmers can concentrate on the business logic. It gives a few short-hand optimizations like pagination column selection. Security features like authorization etc. Create New Query​ To create a new query, follow the following steps: Step 1: Once the editor is loaded and you have selected the app under which the query has to be created, click on the entity from the tree in which you want to create the question. Step 2: Click on the Create button in the left tree and select Query from the menu. Step 3: Fill in the query ID in the input field. Make sure the entity selected should be pre-filled. This query will be added to the specified entity. Make sure you click on the query from the tree once it's created. As it will open the detail section for the query. For naming convention please refer here. Step 4: Once on the query detail page, fill in the required fields like app mode, query type, db selection, and query type. Click here to learn more about each of these. Add Query Property​ Step 1: Click on the Properties tab in the query detail section. And then click on the add (+) icon. Step 2: Fill in the required data such as property ID, property type, domain, length, and other required details. Step 3: Once done with maintaining all data, click on save to persist all data. Step 4: There are multiple tabs, click here to learn more about each of the sections in detail. Once the above steps are completed, the query is ready to use. Delete Query Property​ For deleting a query property, follow these steps: Step 1: Open the Data Studio and select the query in which you want to delete the property. Step 2: Click on the Properties tab and select the properties which you want to delete. Step 3: Click the Delete button in the properties tab toolbar. Click on Delete if it asks for a confirmation. Step 4: Click on the Save button. Entity and Joins​ The entity and joins tab is used to join two or more entities with the help of the JOIN clause. To join two or more entities, follow these steps: Step 1: Click on the Entity and Join tab in the query detail section. Click on add icon(+) Step 2: After clicking the add icon(+), A pop comes to select the root entity (entity to which we are applying the join). Select the root entity and its relation (not mandatory. Only if you want to join the root entity's relation) Step 3: Select the required Join Type. Step 4: Click on Save button Delete a Query​ To delete a query, follow these steps: Step 1: Open the Data Studio and select the app in which you want to delete the query. Step 2: Select the query from the left tree which you want to delete. You can select the query by clicking on the query name in the tree. Once the query is selected, it will enable the detail section. Step 3: Click on the Edit icon in the editor toolbar if the editor is not in editable mode, then click the delete icon. Select OK in the confirmation dialog. Step 4: Click on the Save icon to save the changes and commit them to the DB.

In the Application, ID/key is frequently used to store the related data and at the same time in the user interface, descriptive explanation is required. To achieve it, the ID/key is represented by other single/ multiple data from the related table. Value help is also used to supply the choices available to fill (combo, dropdown, auto-complete) as selection data. Value help can restrict accepting the input value only from valid sets. Create Value Help​ Step 1: Select the entity from the tree in which you want to create the value help. Step 2: Click on the Value Help option from the menu and fill in the Value Help ID. Step 3: Click on Create and then click on the newly created value help from the left tree. This will load the detail section for that value help. Step 4: Fill out all the information in the detail section and click on Save to save all the data. For more information about each of the fields refer to this section. Create VH Trans​ Step 1: Select the entity from the tree in which you want to create the VH Trans. Step 2: Click on the Value Help option from the menu. Step 3: Fill in the Value Help ID and Value Help Type as VH_TRANSACTION. Step 4: Click on Create and then click on the newly created value help from the left tree. This will load the detail section for that value help. Fill out all the required fields. Step 5: Click on the add icon in the Vh Trans field to add vh trans items Note: If we provide is Dependent as true then one more field will get added inside the VH Trans section. Fill out the fields according to your requirements. The descriptions for the fields are explained below: Key: The key is your VH Trans Item ID Display Text: Display text value will display the provided text as the value help item. Icon: The provided icon will also be displayed with the display text Dependent: If a VH Trans item has any dependent value then provide that value to the dependent field. Wherever the dependent item will render, The VH trans item will also render along with that. Lang: It is a language field for your VH item. Step 6: Click on save button to save your vh transaction. ​ Step 1: Select the entity from the tree in which you want to create the VH Trans. Step 2: Click on the Value Help option from the menu. Step 3: Fill in the Value Help ID and Value Help Type as VH_CONFIG Step 4: Click on Create and then click on the newly created value help from the left tree. This will load the detail section for that value help. Fill out all the required fields. Step 5: Click on the add icon in the Vh Config field to add Vh config items. Fill out the key and Display Text field according to your requirements. Step 6: Click on save button to save your vh config. Creating data using Excel Upload: Step 1: Select the value help and click on the Download button. It will excel template. Open that excel file in google sheets. Step 2: Fill the rows with data the user wants to create and download the excel file Step 3: Upload the excel file using the Upload button and select the excel file. It will create the mentioned data and save Delete Value Help​ For deleting a value help, follow these steps: Step 1: Open the Data Studio and select the app in which you want to delete the value help. Step 2: Select the value help from the left tree which you want to delete. You can select the value help by clicking on the value help name in the tree. Once the VH is selected, it will enable the detail section. Step 3: Click on the Edit icon in the editor toolbar if the editor is not in editable mode, then click the delete icon. Select OK in the confirmation dialog. Step 4: Click on the Save icon to save the changes and commit it to the DB.

Permissions is a feature provided to control the access to application resources. By default an application user can access any entity of the application and perform CRUD operation if enabled. To control the access, CRUD permissions can be enabled at entity level and appropriate permissions can be granted to selected users. For more information regarding Permissions refer the below sheet: Permissions - User Guide How to Enable Permissions:​ Step 1: Go to Data Studio, select any flavor and select any entity and select "Access Control" tab Step 2: Click on Edit and turn on the flags as per needed for "Create", "Read", "Update", "Delete" Step 3: Navigate to Permissions screen by clicking on the below link

Row wise authorization is a security feature provided by a framework with which access to entity data can be restricted to selective row items on user level. By default, when a simple select query is fired on any entity, it returns all data that is present in the entity. But, by enabling and configuring row wise authorization on an entity, the list of records accessible to any user can be controlled using access tokens. How to Enable Row Wise Authorization:​ Step 1: Enable the Row Wise Authorization flag. Step 2: Click on add button which will create a new line item. Step 3: Fill the id which is the primary key, access key and then click on the property column icon to add properties. Step 4: Now a dialog will come which will contain all the properties which have been added, by default it will be empty. Now click on add button Step 5: Now select all the properties which need to be added as properties and click on add button Step 6: If sequencing needs to be changed then drag and drop can be done and then click on OK Step 7: Now save the data and a popup will come mentioning if the user wants to recalculate access token, click on OK to continue

Developer AI is an enhancement to the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform that enables users to build enterprise applications by describing their requirements in natural language. Instead of manually configuring application components, users can generate applications through a single prompt, significantly accelerating the application development process.

Developer AI is an AI-powered application development capability built on top of the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform. It transforms business requirements, provided in natural language, into a structured application design and automatically generates the foundational components required to build an enterprise application. Rather than requiring users to manually analyze requirements, design data models, create user interfaces, and configure application components, Developer AI automates these activities using artificial intelligence. This significantly reduces the time and effort involved in the initial stages of application development while ensuring consistency and alignment with business requirements.

When a user provides a business requirement through a prompt, Developer AI performs the following activities: Requirement Understanding Interprets the user's business requirement using Natural Language Processing (NLP). Identifies the business objective, workflows, business entities, users, and relationships. Extracts key functional and data requirements from the provided description. Business Analysis Converts the natural language requirement into structured business insights. Identifies business processes, modules, and system interactions. Determines the application's functional scope and required components. Data Model Generation Analyzes the business entities involved. Identifies attributes, primary keys, foreign keys, and relationships. Generates a normalized data model suitable for the application. Diagram Generation Based on the analyzed requirements, Developer AI automatically generates design artifacts such as: Entity Relationship (ER) Diagram Data Relationship Diagrams Business Process Flow Diagrams Other architecture and visualization diagrams required for application planning These diagrams provide a clear visual representation of the application's structure before development begins. Entity Creation Creates all required business entities. Defines fields, data types, validations, constraints, and relationships. Configures entities according to Procify platform standards. Screen Generation Developer AI automatically generates the application's user interface, including: Data Entry Screens List/Grid Views Detail Pages Forms Navigation structure The generated screens are mapped directly to the underlying business entities and workflows. Dashboard Generation Based on the application's business context, Developer AI creates dashboards containing: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Charts and Graphs Summary Cards Business Metrics Data Visualizations These dashboards provide users with meaningful insights into their business data from the outset. Application Foundation Creation After generating the business model, entities, screens, and dashboards, Developer AI produces the initial application structure within the Procify platform. This foundation serves as the starting point for further customization, refinement, and deployment.

Developer AI is designed to simplify and accelerate enterprise application development by leveraging Artificial Intelligence. It minimizes manual effort in the initial stages of development and enables organizations to transform business ideas into functional applications more efficiently.

Accelerates Application Development Converts business requirements into application components within minutes, significantly reducing development time. Reduces Manual Effort Eliminates the need for manually analyzing requirements, designing data models, and creating initial application structures. Converts Natural Language into Applications Enables users to describe business requirements in plain language, allowing AI to generate the application's foundation automatically. Automates Requirement Analysis Interprets business requirements and extracts key business entities, workflows, relationships, and functional requirements. Generates Design Artifacts Automatically Creates Entity Relationship (ER) diagrams, business process diagrams, and other visual models without manual intervention. Automatically Creates Business Entities Generates entities, attributes, relationships, validations, and data models based on the identified business requirements. Builds User Interface Components Automatically creates forms, screens, list pages, navigation, and dashboards, reducing UI development effort. Ensures Consistency and Standardization Produces applications following Procify platform standards and best practices, ensuring uniformity across projects. Improves Productivity Allows developers to focus on business logic and advanced customizations instead of repetitive setup tasks. Accelerates Time-to-Market Reduces the overall application development lifecycle, enabling organizations to deliver solutions faster. Minimizes Human Errors Automates repetitive design and configuration tasks, reducing the likelihood of manual mistakes. Supports Rapid Prototyping Enables quick creation of application prototypes that can be reviewed, refined, and enhanced based on stakeholder feedback. Enhances Collaboration Provides generated diagrams and structured application models that improve communication between business users, analysts, and developers. Scales with Business Needs Supports the rapid creation of applications of varying complexity while maintaining consistency and quality. Provides a Strong Application Foundation Generates the initial application structure, allowing developers to focus on enhancements, integrations, and business-specific customizations rather than starting from scratch.
