In User Collections, Developer AI needs to be enabled
In App Management, for the App, Developer AI needs to be enabled

We can access Developer AI from chatbot, the chatbot Icon is preset beside notification icon, in Homepage header Note: The chatbot icon is displayed only when Developer AI is enabled for the current landscape. If Developer AI is not enabled, the chatbot icon will not be visible. After click on this chatbot Icon, it will open the chatbot, from there to use the Developer AI, click on “Advanced Mode “ option, which will open the screen for using Developer AI

Step 1 : Upload BRD (Business Requirement Document )​ The Upload Business Requirement Document screen is the first step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this step, users select the target application, review the available AI token quota, and upload the Business Requirement Document (BRD) or Business Blueprint (BBP) that Developer AI will analyze to generate the application. Select Application​ The Select Application dropdown displays all applications, select application with Developer AI enabled the selected application acts as the target application where Developer AI will generate all the required components. All AI-generated artifacts, such as entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, and configurations, are created within the selected application. Ensure the correct application is selected before proceeding with document upload. Note :- 1. Developer AI not Enabled for Application If Developer AI is not enabled for the selected Application, It will show warning that Developer AI is not enabled for that application 2. Developer AI server is not available If the Developer AI Server is not running, a dialog will be displayed with the message: “Developer AI server is currently unavailable. Kindly contact the Administration team.” 3. BBP Build is triggered when other BBP build is in-progress in the same application If Build is triggered in the same application when other BBP Build is in-progress in the same application, then also the warning will come showing the BBP Build is already in progress Token Quota​ The Token Quota section displays the AI token consumption details for the selected user. A token represents a unit of text processed by the AI model. Every analysis performed on a BRD or BBP consumes tokens. The Token Quota panel provides the following information: Tokens Used – Total number of tokens consumed by Developer AI. Total Token Allocation – Maximum tokens allocated to the application. Remaining Tokens – Tokens still available for future AI operations. Usage Percentage – Visual progress bar showing the percentage of the allocated quota that has been consumed. Token Units​ Developer AI displays large token counts using abbreviated units: Unit Meaning Example K Thousand (1,000) 250K = 250,000 tokens M Million (1,000,000) 2.0M = 2,000,000 tokens Example If the Token Quota displays: 2.0M / 26.5M tokens 7% Used 24.5M Remaining It means: A total of 26.5 million tokens have been allocated. 2.0 million tokens have already been consumed. 24.5 million tokens are still available. Approximately 7% of the total token allocation has been utilized. Generate BBP​ The Generate BBP feature enables users to generate a Business Blueprint (BBP) by simply describing their application requirements in natural language. Instead of manually preparing a detailed BBP document, users can provide a high-level business description, and Developer AI automatically transforms it into a structured Business Blueprint. Upload BRD / BBP Document​ Once the application has been selected, upload the project documentation for analysis. Developer AI supports the following documents: Business Requirement Document (BRD) Business Blueprint (BBP) The document can be uploaded by: Dragging and dropping the file into the upload area. Selecting the file from the local system. Once the document is uploaded, Developer AI begins analyzing its contents to understand the business requirements and extract key information required to build the application. During this process, Developer AI identifies and generates: Business entities Functional requirements User roles Application screens Menu structure Business workflows Notifications Schedulers Dashboard requirements Homepage configuration Relationships between business objects The extracted information is then used to automatically generate the initial application structure within the selected Procify application. Preparing a BBP for Developer AI​ Developer AI expects the Business Blueprint (BBP) to follow a predefined structure for accurate analysis and application generation. If your existing BBP is not already in this format, it must be converted before uploading. To prepare a Developer AI-compatible BBP: Ensure you have the existing Business Blueprint (BBP) for your project. Refer to the Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt document (Prompt). Upload both: Your existing BBP. The Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt. Submit both documents to Claude for processing. The conversion prompt has been specifically designed and validated for Claude, and it is recommended not to use other AI models for this conversion. Claude will generate a new BBP that conforms to the standardized format required by Developer AI. Review the generated BBP to verify that the business requirements have been accurately converted. Upload the converted BBP using the Upload Business Requirement Document section to continue the application generation process. Once uploaded, Developer AI will analyze the standardized BBP and generate the application's foundational components, including entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, configurations, and other required artifacts. Step 2 : Analyze & Review​ The Analyze & Review tab is the second step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this stage, Developer AI processes the uploaded BRD or BBP and extracts all the business information required to build the application. The purpose of this step is to validate that the uploaded document has been successfully analyzed before proceeding with application generation. Once the document analysis is completed successfully and the extracted summary has been reviewed, click Open Dashboard to proceed to the detailed review screen. The Open Dashboard button opens the Review Extracted Information dashboard, where users can: Review all extracted business components in detail. Verify entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, schedulers, menu access, and homepage configuration. Modify, add, or remove extracted items as required. Validate the extracted information before proceeding to the Execution Plan stage. Review Extracted Information​ This section provides categorized access to all the information extracted from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Each category displays the number of items identified during the analysis, allowing users to review every component before proceeding with application generation. The available categories include: Entities – Displays the entities extracted from the document. Screens – Lists the application screens identified during analysis. Schedulers – Displays scheduled jobs or background processes. Functional Requirements – Shows the extracted business requirements. Notifications – Lists notification and alert configurations. User Roles – Displays user roles identified for role-based access control. Menu Access – Shows the application's navigation menu structure. Homepage – Displays the extracted homepage configuration. Out of Scope – Lists requirements identified as outside the application's scope. AI Visualize – Provides AI-generated visual representations of the extracted business information. Ask BBP – An AI-powered assistant that answers questions related to the uploaded BBP. Selecting a category displays its corresponding details in the main content area for review. Note: At present, manual addition, modification, or deletion of extracted components is not supported. The entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, and other components displayed on this screen are generated by Developer AI based on the uploaded BRD or BBP and are used as the foundation for application generation. Users can review the extracted information before proceeding to the next step. Export Options​ Developer AI provides an option to export the extracted entity information for offline review or integration. Export to JSON​ The Export to JSON button downloads the extracted entity metadata in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format. The exported file contains structured information such as: Entity details Attributes Relationships Entity types Associated metadata The JSON format can be used for documentation, integration with external systems, or further processing. Export to TXT​ The Export to TXT option is currently not supported. Although the option is visible in the interface, exporting the extracted information in TXT format is not available in the current release and will be supported in a future version.
documents.s: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs

documents.t: The Re-Analyze button allows users to run the document analysis again if changes have been made to the uploaded BRD or BBP, or if the extracted results need to be refreshed. When clicked, Developer AI: Reprocesses the uploaded document. Extracts the latest business requirements and application components. Updates the extracted entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, menu access, and other information.

The Mark All Review Completed button confirms that the extracted information has been reviewed and approved. Selecting this option indicates that: The extracted entities have been verified. Screens and functional requirements have been reviewed. User roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other extracted components have been validated. The application is ready to proceed to the next stage. Note: Marking the review as complete is mandatory before proceeding. If this step is not completed, an alert message will appear when you attempt to continue, prompting you to mark all reviews as completed before moving to the next stage.

The Execution Plan button navigates to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. After the review is completed, clicking Execution Plan opens the Execution Plan screen, where Developer AI displays the sequence of activities required to generate the application. The Execution Plan provides an overview of: Components to be generated. Order of execution. This serves as the final review before Developer AI begins generating the application.

The Refine BBP with AI feature is designed to allow users to improve or modify the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) using natural language instructions before proceeding with application generation. This option can be accessed by clicking the ✨ (AI Refine) button available on the Review Extracted Information screen. How it Works​ Click the ✨ (AI Refine) button. The Refine BBP with AI dialog is displayed. What should AI change? text box, enter the required modifications or enhancements in natural language. Examples: Tighten the module scope. Add missing approval rules. Correct notification triggers. Add a new business entity. Update the workflow for order approval. Click Apply AI Changes. Developer AI is designed to analyze the provided instructions and update the extracted BBP accordingly. The refined information would then be reflected in the extracted components for further review before proceeding with application generation. Note: The Refine BBP with AI feature is currently not supported in the current release. Although the option is available in the interface, AI-based refinement of the extracted BBP is not yet functional and will be supported in a future release. Review BBP Changes Before Build​ After clicking Execution Plan, the Review BBP Changes Before Build dialog is displayed. This screen provides a final summary of the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) before the application build process begins. The summary displays the number of: Existing in BBP – Components that were identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Added – New components that have been added during the review process. Updated – Components that have been modified before execution. The dialog also lists all the extracted application components, such as: Entities Screens Functional Requirements Notifications User Roles Other extracted artifacts This allows users to perform a final verification of the application metadata before proceeding with the build. Available Options Compare AI Changes – Displays a comparison between the original extracted information and any AI-generated changes (if applicable). Back to Review – Returns to the Review Extracted Information screen to make further changes or validations. Proceed to Execution Plan – Confirms the review and navigates to the Execution Plan screen, where the application generation workflow is initiated. Step 3 : Execution Selection​ After clicking Proceed to Execution Plan, the Execution Selection screen is displayed. This screen allows users to review all extracted components and select the items that should be included in the application generation process. A summary at the top of the screen displays the total number of extracted components, including: Entities UI Screens Schedulers Workflows Notifications User Roles Menu Access Homepage Each category shows the number of items identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Component Selection​ The lower section displays the extracted components grouped by category. Each item is accompanied by a checkbox, allowing users to choose whether it should be included in the application build. Users can: Review the extracted entities and screens. Select or deselect individual components. Use the Select All option to include all available components for generation. Only the selected components will be considered during the application generation process. Execute​ After reviewing and selecting the required components, click Execute to start the application generation process. Developer AI begins generating the selected application components within the chosen Procify application. This includes creating the selected entities, screens, workflows, notifications, user roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other supported artifacts. Note: Ensure that all required components are selected before clicking Execute, as only the selected items will be included in the application generation process. Step 4 : Build Application​ After clicking Execute, the Execution Progress screen is displayed. This screen tracks the progress of the application generation process and shows the status of each component being created. To begin generating the application, click Build Application. Build Application​ The Build Application button initiates the application generation process based on the components selected in the Execution Plan. During the build process, Developer AI automatically creates and configures the selected application components, including: Business entities UI screens Value Helps Sample data Application roles Notifications Business rules Menus Homepage configuration Permissions Other supported application artifacts Execution Progress​ As the build progresses, the Execution Progress section displays the status of each component. Each component is marked with one of the following statuses: In Progress – The component is currently being generated. Completed – The component has been successfully created. The progress cards provide a quick overview of the build status for each application component. Execution Log​ The Execution Log records every step performed during the application generation process. The log includes information such as: Analysis completion Entity creation Screen generation Business rule creation Sample data insertion Role creation Menu generation Homepage configuration Permission assignment Any warnings or errors encountered during the build The execution log helps users monitor the build process and troubleshoot issues if required. Build Completed​ When all selected components have been generated successfully, the status changes to Build Completed. A confirmation message indicates that the application has been successfully created within the selected Procify application. Users can then click Continue to proceed to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. Note :- Build Queue Notification When a BBP build is triggered for an application while another BBP build is already in progress for a different application, the new build request is not started immediately. Instead, it is automatically placed in a system-wide queue and will begin execution once the currently running build is completed. Build Already in Progress If a BBP build is triggered for an application that already has an active build in progress, Developer AI does not start a new build for the same application. Instead, it notifies the user that a build is already running and provides an option to view the current build progress. Click Yes, Show Progress to open the ongoing build progress screen, or click Cancel to close the notification

This step will allow users to configure application settings, assign users and roles, manage permissions, customize branding, and define deployment-related configurations before publishing the application.
This step will allow users to validate the generated application, perform publish readiness checks, and publish the application to the target environment.
This step will allow users to generate AI-powered test cases and execute automated Playwright tests to validate the generated application.
This step will allow users to generate AI-powered technical documentation, user guides, configuration guides, and downloadable project documentation for the generated application.
This step will allow users to review the final application generation summary, verify the completed workflow, and conclude the Developer AI application generation process.

Entities After the application is generated, all the business entities created by Developer AI are automatically available in the Data Studio. These entities form the core data model of the generated application and can be reviewed and further configured as needed. The left navigation panel displays the list of all generated entities. Selecting an entity opens its complete configuration, where you can review its properties, relationships, business rules, workflows, access control, and other metadata. Note: If the generated entities are not immediately visible in the Data Studio, refresh the application or browser. The entities will be displayed once the latest metadata is loaded. Screens Developer AI automatically generates the required application pages based on the uploaded BRD/BBP. These pages provide the user interface for interacting with the generated business entities and application features. The generated pages are available in the Page Builder and can be reviewed, customized, or enhanced using the standard Procify page designer. In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following pages: p_homepage_001 – The application's landing page that provides users with the initial view after logging in. p_dashboard_001 – Displays the application's dashboard, providing a consolidated view of key information, widgets, and business insights. p_delivery_mgmt – The Delivery Management page used to create, view, update, and manage delivery-related transactions. Role & Users The roles and users generated by Developer AI can be viewed from the Roles & Users section under the Details tab of the generated application in App Management. This section allows you to review the user roles and user assignments created for the application. Homepage Log in using one of the users created in the Roles & Users section. After successful login, the application opens the Homepage generated by Developer AI. The homepage displayed corresponds to the configuration defined in the Homepage component during the application generation process. It serves as the application's landing page and provides users with quick access to the generated modules, dashboards, and navigation menus based on their assigned role and permissions. Dashboard Developer AI automatically generates the application dashboard based on the requirements defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP. The generated dashboard provides users with a consolidated view of key business information, metrics, and navigation components relevant to the application. It is designed to offer quick access to important data and frequently used features immediately after login. The dashboard created by Developer AI can be accessed from the Dashboard menu within the generated application and can be further customized using the standard Procify dashboard designer to meet specific business requirements. Note: The layout, widgets, and overall design of the generated dashboard are determined by Developer AI based on its analysis of the uploaded BBP or BRD. Dashboard generation is AI-driven, and users cannot control or define the dashboard layout by providing screenshots or sample designs. To influence the generated dashboard, include clear and detailed dashboard requirements within the BBP or BRD. Menu Developer AI automatically generates the application's navigation menu based on the modules, screens, and user workflows defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP. The generated menu provides users with organized navigation to access the application's features. Menu items are created based on the business requirements and are assigned appropriate access according to the generated user roles and permissions. In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following menu items: Home – The default landing page that provides users with quick access to the application. My Deliveries – A module for managing and viewing delivery-related transactions. Dashboard – Provides access to the application's dashboard, displaying key business insights and summary information.

This document provides a complete guide for enabling and using Git integration within the Procify platform. It explains how to configure GitHub or Bitbucket repositories, set up SSH access, connect them to your Procify flavor, and work with Git-based version control during development. It covers the end-to-end process—including repository setup, user access, configuring Git details in the Workspace Hub, checking out flavors, and using Git-linked workflows within the Procify environment.

1️⃣ Create a Repository under your Organization​ Go to GitHub. Click “New repository” → create it under your organization account (not personal). Example organization: procify-vsix-integration(only one time setup required by respective app manager) 3️⃣ Invite the procify_github User​ Go to your organization → People / Members section. Click Invite member → invite procify_github. Add procify_user to this organisation https://github.com/orgs/organization_name/people ![][image1] Give read-only access to the repository (permission = Read). Example repo name: EMS Do select .gitignore with Node ![][image2] Then add these things in your .gitignore # Build-generated directories metadata/ entity_gen/ query_gen/ Tsconfig.json Your .gitignore should look like this ![][image3]

1️⃣ Create a Repository under your Organization​ Go to Bitbucket. Click Create Repository. Make sure you create it under your team/workspace, not your personal space. Example workspace: procify_test Example repo: rps → Path: https://bitbucket.org/procify_test/rps 2️⃣ Create a Branch​ In Bitbucket UI or terminal: git checkout -b your_branch_name git push origin your_branch_name Do commit a .gitignore with following contents # Build-generated directories metadata/ entity_gen/ query_gen/ Tsconfig.json 3️⃣ Invite the procify_bitbucket User​ Go to your workspace → Repository settings → User and group access. Note:before adding here you will need to add procify_bitbucket to yourworkspace(one time) Click Add user. Add procify_bitbucket. Set Access level = Read (read-only). How to enable the feature For github: 4️⃣ Copy the SSH URL (⚠️ Not HTTPS)​ Go to your repo in GitHub. Click the “Code” (green button). Select the “SSH” tab. Copy the SSH URL ( will looks like this): git@github.com:procify-vsix-integration/phenotest_app.git ​ 5️⃣ Add Repo Details in Workspace Hub​ In your Procify Workspace Hub, fill these fields: Note: There are two values for github fill procify_github, for bitbucket fill procify_bitbucket: After filling alias repourl and Git Branch click on verify, if you get any error like this Then contact admin; Field Value r_git_repourl git@github.com:procify-vsix-integration/EMS.git r_git_branch (your branch name, e.g., main, test_branch, etc.) r_git_alias procify_github ✅ Then click Verify, you should get this response Then click on save Note:- for existing flavor first create one private node and copy the whole flavor(where you want to integrate git), then fill repo details in Workspace Hub and also make sure all developers using this flavor should have write access of corresponding github/bitbucket repo & that branch For bitbucket: 4️⃣ Copy the SSH URL (⚠️ Not HTTPS)​ Go to the repo → click Clone. Select the SSH option. Copy the SSH URL, e.g.: git@bitbucket.org:procify_test/rps.git 5️⃣ Add Repo Details in Workspace Hub​ Fill the details like this: Field Value r_git_repourl git@bitbucket.org:procify_test/rps.git r_git_branch (your branch name, e.g., main, develop, etc.) r_git_alias Procify_bitbucket ✅ Then click Verify, you should get this response Then click on save Note: There are two values for github fill procify_github, for bitbucket fill procify_bitbucket: After filling alias repourl and Git Branch click on verify, if you get any error like this Then contact admin; Note:- for existing flavor first create one private node and copy the whole flavor(where you want to integrate git), then fill repo details in Workspace Hub and also make sure all developers using this flavor should have write access of corresponding github/bitbucket repo & that branch

SN Steps 1 Go to privateNode and after doing registration you will get one popup to enter bitbucket_details (Click on cancel it if you don’t have any repository with bitbucket configured. Otherwise fill in this way First create an apitoken from bitbucket https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens There create token Select Create API token with scopes Set expires on date to next year In select app section select bitbucket Click on create_token Copy this apikey and save it to same safe_place and now come back to privatenode Note:- also copy your username which you can get here https://bitbucket.org/account/settings/ Fill it here in this manner Click on save Credentials and then move to checkout(don’t checkout before if your flavor is git configured) Order should be first fill details then checkout, GITHUB If you have github configured: Then go to command palette(for windows click F1 & for mac Command + Shift + P)) Then search for klobasegithub Click on that and then it will ask for allow If you have already logged in through github then it will show there only, you can select, if not then choose select other account it will open in browser and there select github account

Note: by default it will checkout from branch which is configured, but there might be case that you don’t have valid access of that branch, so before doing any change checkout that branch. For gitconfigured flavors any change made will not show in existing button(commit All) so you can’t save your changes to public via that button, for committing your change to public commit to corresponding git branch ⚠️ Note — newly created files: The above applies to changes to existing files. When you create a new file (controller / entity / query / rules / view), the Private Node save still records it in the app so it appears in your file explorer — but Build & Deploy reads these file types only from your Git repository, never from the app database. You must commit and push the new file to Git — even if it still holds just the initial template it was scaffolded with — before running Build & Deploy. Skipping this step causes the build to succeed with no warning, but the file will be missing from the deployed app, and the screen using it will fail to load at runtime.
documents.s: After successful checkout you can change your branch from vscode ui or by git commands:

documents.t: Before releasing an app create a tag in that app via private node and push it to origin ( can be done via following ways: git tag -a 1-0-1 -m "Releasing 1-0-1" git push origin 1-0-1 Now go to Workspace Hub and click on edit and add this tag there 1-0-1 Click on verify to check if tag is already there, now click on save and then you can release Note: never add that tag if you are not going to release that app (while build it will take data till that tag only), make sure that git tag is created after last commit in that repository.
If you create one branch of app and that app is git configured then try to create one branch in that repo and add that branch in Workspace Hub
All repo related details will be copied from the previous version.

Q: Checkout Not Working for Git-Configured Apps​ A: Open a new Command Prompt (CMD) window and verify the configured Git username and email: git config --global user.name git config --global user.email If no values are returned, configure them using: git config --global user.name "Your Name" git config --global user.email "your.email@example.com" After configuring the Git user details, retry the checkout operation. Q: A newly created controller/entity/query/rules file works in the Private Node but the screen fails to load ("module not found") after Build & Deploy​ A: The file was created but never committed/pushed to the configured Git repository. Build & Deploy sources these file types exclusively from Git, so a file that exists only in the app is not present in the build output. Commit and push the file (even with just its initial template) to the configured branch, then re-run Build & Deploy. If the file is no longer needed, delete it from within Klobase so the stale entry is cleaned up — otherwise the same error recurs on every build.

The Procify Landing Page Settings provides a robust, secure, and performant solution for creating dynamic homepage experiences. By following this documentation and implementing the recommended best practices, developers can create powerful, user-friendly homepage systems that scale with organizational needs while maintaining security and performance standards. For additional support or advanced configuration requirements, consult the Procify development team or refer to the latest API documentation. Note: KloGuid and KloLink controls will be disabled when added inside the embedded subscreens. Since the homepage uses embedded sections to display the screens, they will appear to be disabled as well. If required please use sap.m.Link control.

Need Landing Page Settings to be assigned as TESTER NOTE: For existing applications, a migration script is given to fill the title of the homepage with the title of the screen to show in the tab. It is recommended to do the flavor build once so that the title will reflect in the UI.

SN Steps 1 Assign the homepage_editor as a TESTER to yourself Go to Procify Workspace Hub and assign the latest version of homepage_editor flavor to yourself as a tester. 2 Go to the Landing Page Settings Once assigned, you will get the Upgrade Banner. Once you get the upgrade banner and registration is complete, Click the Hamburger menu and select App Builder Menu Header. Select Landing Page Settings from the Menu. You will be Navigated to the Landing Page Settings. Note: The Edit button will be disabled if no flavor is selected from the drop down. 3 Make sure you are in bolversion 7-2-227 or Higher Note: You can check this from the about page 4. Select the flavor to create/see the homepages in that flavor. Once you select the flavor, the edit button will be enabled. If there are homepages in that flavor that will appear in the list. Once you have selected the flavor, it will persist even if you refresh and homepages in that flavor will be persisted 5. Click the Edit button to go into Edit Mode Once you Click the Edit button, the page will go to Edit Mode. You should now be able to see Add, Delete, Save and Cancel Buttons. 6 Click On Home Icon below the Hamburger Menu in the sidebar to navigate to Home Page If you have not added any Homepage entries in the Landing Page Settings, then Procify Logo with Procify text is shown below it 7 Click on + Add button A new homepage entry will be created Fill in the screen id in the page column by clicking the Value Help Icon and selecting the screen you like. Fill in the sequence and Tab Text. Click on Save. Once Save is successful the page will reload and You can click the Homepage button again to see the added Home Page. If one Homepage entry is added, then that homepage is shown in the screen. 8 Add another Homepage in another flavor Go to Landing Page Settings and Select a different flavor, Click on Edit to Go Into Edit mode. Click on +Add button. Fill the screen id and changed the Tab Text if you want. Go to the homepage. If there are more than one entries in homepage, then You will see a tab with icon and title (icon filled from the tab_icon and title will be filled from the tab_text fields of the Landing Page Settings) In Mobile, back button is removed and the title in the screen titlebar will be dynamically updated based on the currently selected tab and filled from the title property of the Landing Page Settings, if not provided then picked from the Tab Text otherwise screenid. Precedence: Tab Text=> Screen Title => Screen Id Precedence: Title => Tab Text => Screen Id If no homepages are added then the title “Home” is shown in the screen title bar. 9 Now in the roles field, select the role other than the role currently assigned to the user Here the app is assigned as TESTER to the user but we are selecting as manager Since the role doesn’t match, the screen is not shown to the user i.e., it is hidden from the user. 10 Add permissions to your entity Create a permission group in Role Permissions if it doesn’t exist Enable Excel Download permission for testing purpose. Then Go to Landing Page Settings and In Edit Mode, Select the required permission from the Permissions dropdown. Then if the permissions is valid, then the Homepage is Visible otherwise it won’t be visbile NOTE: Make sure that all the permissions are assigned for all the users by default, even after assigning the permissions to the homepage and permission not given and homepage is still showing up then remove the permission group “flv_master_grp” from the Role Permissions screen for your user role. 11 You can trim the subscreen by passing Page Parameters. Eg: {"trimSubscreen": "s_notif_t_detail"}. Here s_notif_t_detail is the detail section’s subscreenid 12 We can change the Icon which is shown in the Tab of the HomeScreen.

Middleware (Message Monitoring) is an application that is used for fetching all the information about the entries that are present in the device Info or tenant Info. We can also reprocess the failed messages present inside the error_q of the tenant. Device Info: When we are sending any data/action from server to device we store the message in the device info to know its information and state. In device info, every message is an outgoing message. So, the successfully sent messages are shown here. So, It goes from In queue to success. Tenant Info: When we are sending/fetching any data/action from server to SAP LOCAL or sending data from device to server. We store the message in tenant info to know its information and state. All the messages from Device to Server and SAP Local to server are visible in Inbound MessagesServer Queue Monitor screen. All the messages from Server to SAP Local will be visible to the Outbound queue screen and all the messages from server to device or SAP Local to device will be visible in Device OutboundDevice Queue Monitor screen. Purpose of Message Monitoring​ Message Monitoring is used to show information about messages (UPGRADE, DEBOARD) and the state of the message whether it's in the in-queue, Success, or failed. Every message has a state out of the three states mentioned below : In-Queue: The message is ready for processing. Success: The message has been processed successfully. Failed: Message processing has failed. We can also reprocess the Failed message. The reprocess function is only available for tenant_q. When we are sending/fetching any data/Action from server to device or server to SAP local, we store it in terms of messages to know its information and its state. Navigate to Message Monitoring​ Step 1: Go to the Operations MonitorSystem Monitor option Go to the menu options and select Operations MonitorSys Monitor. Step 2: Click on the required option Click on either Inbound MessagesServer Queue Monitor (Tenant Info**)** or Device OutboundDevice Queue Monitor (Device Info**)** according to your requirements. What type of data will be stored in message monitoring tables:​ It will store the messages for all the transactional data changes. NOTE: Metadata changes will not be reflected in the message monitoring screens.

When we are sending any data/action from server to device, we store the message in the device info to know its information and state. In device info, every message is sent or is in the process of being successfully sent. So, every message is outgoing and never fails. Hence, It goes from in-queue to success. 1.1.1. Screen​ The below image shows the filter: Fields Description Target Endpoint This implies a destination Endpoint. App This implies a destination app. Created from and Created To This takes the date range from which we want the entries to be loaded till a particular range that we have selected in our application. The search result will be shown as: The Device Info screen has three preview sections i.e. Success, In-Queue, and Failed. These are described as follows: Fields Description Success This section shows all items that were successfully processed. In-Queue This section shows all the data that are currently present in the device_q and which are not processed yet. After processing, either the entries will move to device_log_q (success) or device_error_q (failed). Failed This section shows all entries that failed while processing. The section at the top shows: Fields Description In-Queue The count of new or in-queued messages. Success The count of processed messages. Failed The count of error messages The below section shows the count of the target endpoint and endpoint status present on the selected tab (Success, In-Queue or error). For Endpoints, Fuzzy search will work for: Target Endpoint in Device Outbounddevice queue monitor. Target Endpoint and source endpoint in tenant queue monitor. An Upsert operation refers to the combination of update and insert actions, where data is either updated if it exists or inserted if it doesn't. When syncing messages, an Upsert scenario behavior typically involves checking if a message already exists in the destination system or database. If it exists, the system will update it; if it doesn't, the system will insert it as a new record. 1.5.1.Upsert Behavior in Middleware for Syncing Messages:​ Data Creation and Update: If the data is new (does not exist in the system), a new entry will be created. If the data already exists, the existing record will be updated instead of creating a new one. Upsert for Root Business Objects (BOs) and Primary Relations: Upsert is only applicable for Root Business Objects (BOs) and their primary relations. For non-primary relations, the Upsert operation will work only if the relation is established using primary keys. Parent-Child Relationship: If a parent is new, but the child data related to the parent already exists, this is considered an unexpected scenario. The user must handle this manually, as it is not automatically managed by the middleware. 1.5.2.Delete Scenario Behavior:​ Parent Entity Deletion: If the parent entity is deleted, the child entities will only be deleted if the user explicitly sends the isdeleted flag as true in the request body for both the parent and child entities. This applies to both primary and aggregate relationships. Child Entity Deletion: If the child entity is deleted, only the child will be deleted. The parent entity will remain intact.

Messages that are failed to process can be found in the error q. The error can be found in the error message. Possible reasons a message can fail are. Application logic - When an application logically rejects a request for processing the message. I.e. Adding items to a closed order. Adding shipments to a closed Delivery etc. Suggested solution : Find the root cause why these messages are generated. Eg. screen still allows adding items even if the status of order is closed. And fix the issue / add validation in the client side also. Application bugs - Some cases where application code has a bug, due to which an exception can be raised the message will fail. Eg. Improper null handling, wrong API parameters, typo etc. Transaction User not configured - File processing, transaction user has to be configured with required application & permissions. As all the messages are processed based on the access of the user, messages generated by files need a user to validate against. Refer to the Landscape Editor for how to configure the transaction user. Configured user doesn’t have application assigned : When messages from SAP / File processing are failing with “Access denied: user lacks permission to the required application.” error, it means, the user (SAP communication user / File processing user) does not have that flavor assigned to them. Database Deadlock / Lock Timeout Errors: - When the middleware encounters a transient database deadlock or lock wait timeout (e.g., "Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction"), messages are automatically retried up to 3 times with a 1-second delay (default values) between attempts. - If all retries are exhausted, the message will move to the error queue. - It will have an error message like - "Message <msg_id> failed after 3 retry attempts due to Lock wait timeout exceeded" or "Message <msg_id> failed after 3 retry attempts due to Deadlock found". - The retry settings are configurable via config.json: "MiddlewareRetrySettings": { "DeadlockRetryCount": 3, "RetryDelaySeconds": 1 }

When an application team logs in from multiple or random devices without properly deboarding the previous devices, those devices can continue to be considered active endpoints. As a result, messages may continue to be generated for these endpoints even though the application team is no longer actively using them. Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Whenever any new user registers in the application, a new endpoint ID is created against that account... when they log in again the status becomes Active." Each login is a distinct endpoint; none are deregistered automatically on crash or app closure.
documents.s: 2.1. Multiple Logins Can Create Active Endpoints

documents.t: Because these endpoints remain active, messages generated for them may not be synchronized with the device immediately. Over time, a large number of messages can accumulate in the queue. This can give the impression that a large number of messages are stuck. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — In-Queue is defined as "all the data that are currently present in the device_q and which are not processed yet." A high In-Queue count reflects endpoints awaiting sync, not failed or lost messages.
documents.s: 2.2 Messages Can Accumulate in the Queue

documents.t: When the corresponding device comes online , the queued messages are synchronized with the device. Once the server successfully sends the messages and receives the required acknowledgment from the client, the messages move to Success. If the device is offline, the messages remain in the queue until the device becomes available. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — device_q entries move to device_log_q (Success) or device_error_q (Failed) only after processing; until then they remain In-Queue, consistent with holding messages for an offline device until it reconnects.
documents.s: 2.3. Messages Are Synchronized When the Device Becomes online

documents.t: A message can reach the device successfully, but the actual processing on the device may still fail. From the server's perspective, the message can be marked as Success when the client acknowledges that the message was received while the device was online. Therefore, Success on the server does not necessarily mean that the message was successfully processed by the application on the device. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — "In device info, every message is sent or is in the process of being successfully sent. So, every message is outgoing and never fails. Hence, It goes from in-queue to success." This confirms Success tracks the send/acknowledgment, not on-device application processing.

The application team may not be aware that previously used devices are still registered as active endpoints. This can result in messages continuing to be generated and queued for those endpoints. Note: This is a training/visibility gap rather than a platform defect. Recommend making Sections 1–4 of this topic available to application teams so "stuck message" reports can be self-diagnosed before being escalated as incidents.

A scheduler runs every Sunday to clean up old endpoints. Note: The scheduler currently deboards endpoints that have been inactive for more than 7 days. Once an endpoint is deboarded, its corresponding entry is removed from the endpoint table. Property Value Class name deboardInactiveUsers CRON expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN * (every Sunday at midnight) Current inactivity threshold (this environment) 7 days Platform default threshold 15 days — this environment has been configured below the default Channel type BOTH, unless restricted to DEVICE or BROWSER Table cleaned up Endpoint's entries removed from madm_ep_apps Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Deboard Inactive Users": CRON Job Expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN *, class deboardInactiveUsers, parameters No_of_inactive_days {default: 15} and Channel_type {default: BOTH}; "this scheduler will deboard all the users who are inactive since given days and it will delete the entry of all deboarded endpoints from madm_ep_apps."

If the default 7-day cleanup period does not meet the application's requirements, the scheduler can be customized to use a different endpoint deboarding period. To change it: Go to the job-instances page in Cockpit and locate the deboardInactiveUsers job. Open the job instance's parameters. Update No_of_inactive_days to the desired threshold. Update Channel_type if the cleanup should be restricted to a specific channel. Save. The new threshold takes effect on the job's next scheduled run (the following Sunday, per the fixed CRON expression). Note: The CRON schedule itself (currently fixed to Sunday) is a separate setting from the inactivity threshold — changing how often the job runs, as opposed to how many inactive days it waits, would need to be confirmed as in-scope for this customization request.

Overview The Middleware Message Forwarding feature allows you to automatically sync data changes between different flavors of your application. When data is changed in one flavor (source), it can automatically trigger message generation for users of another flavor (target), ensuring all users stay synchronized regardless of which flavor they're using.

Application Architecture Requirements​ Multi-Flavor Setup​ ✅ You must have multiple flavors (source and target flavors) ✅ Both source and target flavors must be deployed and accessible ✅ Flavors should share common entities that require message sync Entity Design​ ✅ Target Entity: Must exist with identical entity name and table name ✅ Target Entity: Must have ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event configured with proper implementation Access and Permissions​ Administrative Access​ ✅ Access to Operations Monitor application for configuration ✅ Permissions to create/modify Middleware Message Routing entries ✅ Message monitoring access for troubleshooting and monitoring Development Environment​ ✅ Private node setup with DEV landscape (for testing) ✅ Access to both source and target flavor codebases ✅ Debugging capabilities in development environment Technical Prerequisites​ Message Processing Infrastructure​ ✅ Message processing must be functional Monitoring Tools​ ✅ Message Monitoring screen access for tracking forwarded messages ✅ Queue Monitor for viewing message queues and error queues ✅ Log access for troubleshooting and debugging Knowledge Requirements​ Development Team​ ✅ Understanding of entity event implementation (ENDPOINT_RESOLVER) ✅ Familiarity with addEndpoint() method usage ✅ Knowledge of message queue and processing ✅ Experience with multi-flavor application development Configuration Team​ ✅ Understanding of flavor versioning and deployment ✅ Knowledge of landscape management (DEV/TEST/PROD) ✅ Familiarity with Operations Monitor configuration tools

Setting Up Flavor Mapping​ To enable message forwarding, you need to configure mappings in the Mw Message Routing Screen in Operations Monitor: Configuration Screen - Mw Message Routing Access this screen through Operations Monitor > Middleware Message Routing Required Fields​ Source Flavor: The flavor where changes originate Target Flavor: The flavor that where the changes should be also be forwarded for message generation. Is Active: Set to true to enable forwarding Target Version: Only for DEV Specify a particular version of the target flavor. Use this for debugging purposes. In QA & Production, the latest version is used. Configuration Steps​ Open Operations Monitor application Navigate to "Middleware Message Routing" Click "Add New" to create a mapping Fill in Source Flavor and Target Flavor names Set "Is Active" to true Save the configuration

Common Use Cases​ Multi-Flavor Applications​ If your application has multiple flavors (e.g., online and offline versions) that share common entities, this feature ensures data consistency across all flavors. Example Scenarios:​ Portal + Mobile App: Changes made in the web portal should sync to mobile app users Hierarchical Applications: Parent flavor changes should sync to child flavor users How Does It Work ?​ Data Change Trigger: When you create, update, or delete data in a source flavor Automatic Detection: The system detects if forwarding is configured for that flavor in Middleware Message Routing ( Operations Monitor ) Trigger Endpoint Resolver: The ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event will be triggered in target flavor if the same entity exists. Message Generation: Messages are generated for target flavor users based on the target flavor ENDPOINT_RESOLVER logic. Synchronized Delivery: All related messages share the same reference ID for tracking Entity Requirements​ Target Entity Setup​ Your target entity must have:​ Same entity name as source entity Same table name (tb field) as source entity ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event configured Event implementation in the entity class file Example Entity Event Implementation​ // In your entity class file (e.g., src/flavor/entity/your_entity.ts) async onEndpointResolver(txn, dataObj, headers) { // Your logic to determine which users/endpoints should receive messages this.addEndpoint(userList, EndpointType.User, ChannelType.Both); } Testing in Private Node​ 1. Setup Test Environment​ Set up your private node with DEV landscape Checkout the source flavor and required target flavors. If target flavor is not present in the private node, forwarding will be skipped. Create test flavor mappings with specific target versions 2. Create Test Data​ Perform create, update, delete operations on the source entity 3. Debugging​ You can debug the target flavor entity event implementation by setting breakpoints in your private node. 4. Monitor Message Flow​ Messages generated during forwarding will have:​ Same ref_msg_id for all related messages src_fv field showing source flavor version dst_fv field showing target flavor version

Checking Message Forwarding Status​ Use the Message Monitoring screen to track forwarded messages and verify successful processing: The forwarding status icon in the message monitoring screen indicates when messages have been forwarded Understanding Forwarding Status​ Icon Appearance: Look for the forwarding indicator next to messages Status Information: Click the icon to see detailed forwarding information Detailed view showing forwarding status and target flavor information Tracking Related Messages by Reference ID​ All messages from the same transaction share a reference ID for easy tracking: Reference ID icon allows you to view all related messages from the same transaction Using Reference ID Tracking​ Locate the Reference ID icon in the message list Click to expand and view all related messages Verify both source and target flavor messages are present Expanded view showing all messages sharing the same reference ID Troubleshooting Failed Forwards​ When message forwarding fails, check the Error Queue for detailed information: Error queue entry showing failed forwarding message with MSG_FORWARD type Error Queue Analysis​ Message Type: Look for "MSG_FORWARD" type entries Error Details: Review error messages for troubleshooting Retry Options: Use message reprocessing to retry failed forwards Behavioral Changes to Expect​ Message Generation​ Additional Messages: You'll see target flavor messages in device/tenant queues Message Grouping: Related messages share the same reference ID Cross-Flavor Sync: Changes in source flavor should trigger messages in target flavor Error Handling​ Isolated Failures: If target flavor processing fails, source transaction still completes Error Queue Entries: Failed forwards create entries in error queue with type MSG_FORWARD Retry Capability: Failed messages forwarding can be reprocessed later. It will only retry the forwarding, not the original transaction. The dirty state and from state is preserved from the original transaction. Understanding Message Reference IDs​ What is a Reference ID?​ The reference ID (ref_msg_id) is a unique identifier that groups all messages generated from a single transaction. How It Works​ Original Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" ├── Source Flavor Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" ├── Target Flavor 1 Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" └── Target Flavor 2 Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" Detecting Forwarded Messages​ In your entity event handlers, you can detect if the event was triggered by message forwarding: async onEndpointResolver() { let headers = await this.getHeaders(); let sourceApp = headers.src_app; let currentFlavor = this.txn.$SYSTEM.flavor; if (sourceApp !== currentFlavor) { // This event was triggered by message forwarding this.info(`Message forwarded from ${sourceApp} to ${currentFlavor}`); } else { // This is a normal event execution } }

Configuration Management​ Minimal Mappings: Only configure necessary flavor mappings Environment-Specific: Use similar configurations for DEV/TEST/PROD Regular Review: Periodically audit your forwarding configurations Testing Strategy​ Verify End-to-End: Test complete data flow from source to target users Monitor Queues: Watch queue growth during testing Check Error Logs: Review error queues for any issues Troubleshooting Common Issues​ Messages Not Forwarding​ Checklist: ✅ Mapping exists in Msg Forward Mapping ✅ r_is_active is set to true ✅ Target entity exists with same name and table ✅ Target flavor entities have ENDPOINT_RESOLVER events ✅ If private node is used, make sure target flavor is assigned. Using Message Monitoring Tools:​ Check the forwarding status icon in Message Monitoring Look for error entries in Error Queue with MSG_FORWARD type Verify Reference ID grouping shows both source and target messages Review detailed forwarding information in status dialogs Monitoring and Maintenance​ Regular Checks​ Queue Monitoring: Review device and tenant queue sizes Error Analysis: Check error queues for failed forwards Maintenance Tasks​ Error Queue Cleanup: Process and resolve failed messages Configuration Updates: Modify mappings as application evolves Documentation Updates: Keep mapping documentation current Getting Help​ Support Information​ When contacting support, provide:​ Source and target flavor names/versions Entity name and table name Reference ID of problematic messages Relevant error log entries Current mapping configuration

What is kloTouch? kloBase platform is a modern low-code platform to build enterprise-class cloud-enabled portals and mobile business applications. Its unique layered development empowers to build powerful reusable models for the continuously evolving business needs. kloTouch is a low-code visual designer tool that helps application development efficiently and effectively. What is the objective of kloTouch? kloTouch is a visual designing Page Builder that is effective in building applications that work on portals and mobile applications. kloTouch has the following objectives: Ease of Operating: It involves least to no complex coding, thus, making it an easy-to-use tool, not only for the modellers but also for common people with limited technical knowledge. Efficient: This Page Builder is programmed in a manner that requires a limited to negligible coding process. This prevents the modellers and developers from losing time by writing lengthy codes, thus saving time. Rich In-Built Features: Multiple add-ons and real-time notifications to name a few, help make it a featureful application.
The App selection drop-down contains a list of apps that have been assigned to the user. By using the drop-down users can select the app on which they are going to work.

The page selection drop-down is used to select the page. The page dropdown will list all the pages available for the app that have been selected. Note:This drop-down will be visible only when the app is selected.
The Create Page has three parts: Create Blank Page Create a Page From Wizard Update Page From Wizard Make A Copy of Page The Create page option is to create a new page for the selected app.
The undo option is to revert the changes that were made. The use of the redo option is to redo the changes that are undone.
The painter can be used to copy a property or style or vienable of one control to another/multiple controls.

Step 1: Select any control/section from the page tree section Step 2: select the option from the painter Property - all the property details of the selected item will be copied Style - all the styles added to the selected item will be copied Vienable - all the vienable applied to the selected property will be copied Step 3: Now select the control/section in the page tree to which the copied items should be pasted. Note: With the painter option, we can apply the copied items to multiple elements, so once the items are pasted, click on `Esc`.
The Save option is used to save the changes that are done. Note:Save button will be visible only in edit mode. The Edit option is used to make the kloEditor modifiable.

The Read-Only and Cancel option is only visible in editable mode. Clicking read-only mode locks the editor in making further changes. On click of the cancel icon, any changes made in the editor that are not yet saved will be reverted.

Properties​ The property tab in the detail section displays the properties that are added and options to add new properties that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, pageLayout, sections, controls). Refer to this to understand binding concepts. Value:​ The value field will hold the value provided for the property. Path:​ In this path field, users can only bind with exactly one property or value. Type:​ In the type field, the user can provide the datatype for the control’s value. Formatter Options:​ Formatter options define how a value is formatted and displayed in the UI. Validation Constraint:​ Constraints are optional and define how an input value that is entered in the UI should look like. During parsing, the value is validated against these constraints. For example, an Integer type has a constraint for the maximum that is automatically validated when parsing the input values. Default Page Data Models:​ KloTouch module of Framework is providing default Page Data Models: Properties Usage deviceInfo Indicates user’s device type with Boolean values for properties: desktop, tablet, phone Example Binding: {= ${$M>/deviceInfo/desktop} } $M: Model deviceInfo: Page Data Model Desktop: Property perm Contains all enabled permissions in app Example Binding: {= ${$M>/perm/d_sales=CR_ACC} } $M: Model perm: Page Data Model d_sales=CR_ACC: Getter for Create permission enabled in entity d_sames which returns Boolean value env_user Contains all Env User Properties Example Binding: {= ${$M>/env_user/owning_bp} !== 'BP001' ? true : false } $M: Model env_user: Page Data Model role: One of the properties of Env User env_system Contains all System Data(transaction.$SYSTEM) Properties Example Binding: {= ${$M>/env_system/roleID} !== 'DEVELOPER' ? true : false } $M: Model env_system: Page Data Model role: One of the properties of System Data(transaction.$SYSTEM) ​
The page refers to the single visible screen of the application. The page is the topmost layer of an application. It will be embedded with a pageLayout.

Create Blank Page: Step 1 - Select the Add icon to create a Blank Page To create a new page click on the Add icon from the top toolbar. Three options will be shown, from those options select ‘Create Blank Page’. After selecting the option a popup will be displayed. Step 2 - Fill the popup to create a new page In the popup, provide the ID and name/title for the new page. After providing the details, click on the Submit button. Note: Newly created pages will be updated in the database only after saving. To save click on the save icon at the top toolbar (right side of the edit action button). Supporting layouts are Grid Layout Default Dialog Fit To Area Flexible Column (Deprecated, Use Two Column Pagelayout Instead) Horizontal Splitter Object Page Stack Sticky Tab Tiles Vertical Splitter. It allows users to visualize relationships between parent and child nodes, making it ideal for displaying nested information such as organisational charts, file systems, or any other hierarchical datasets. Implementation: Data Preparation:​ To prepare the data for a Tree Screen Type, we will use a JSON format that represents the hierarchical structure. Here’s a sample JSON array: [{ "key_01": "value_1", "key_02": "value_2", "key_03": "value_3", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_11", "key_02": "value_22", "key_03": "value_33", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_111", "key_02": "value_222", "key_03": "value_333", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_1111", "key_02": "value_2222", "key_03": "value_3333", }] }] }] }] JSON Structure Each object represents a node in the tree. The child array holds nested objects, representing the child nodes. Key names for child nodes are consistent with parent nodes, ensuring a clear relationship. We will store the data in other type transnode. Screen:​ Step 1: Create one pageArea with screentype, fit_to_area and a section with screentype, tree. Step 3: Add Controls for Data Binding Create controls within the section for each key in your JSON data (key_01, key_02, key_03). Bind the section to the other type transnode that contains the hierarchical JSON data. Ensure that each control is correctly bound to the corresponding key in the JSON structure. By using this embedded section we can embed sections or containers from other pages to our current page. Note: KloGuid and KloLink controls will be disabled when added inside the embedded subscreens. Also, the title, icon and actions provided for the embedded subscreen will not be rendered. Page layout type” flexible_col” is not supported inside embedded section.

To create an embedded page create a page Layout in the page where the section is embedded from. In our current page create an embedded section. In the layout data of the embedded section provide the value below: flavor.pageId.pageContainerId if it's a separate app. pageId.pageContainerId if the embedding page is from the same app. Note: Developers can pass supported navTo() properties from a parent screen to an embedded child screen. TN and NT parameters will be passed to child functions (such as onPageEnter() and onSectionEnter()) only when they are explicitly maintained in the embedded section's screenParameters configuration.
The properties available in the embedded config are listed below. Embedded config can be added from context menu of the embedded section

NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION flavor string - App from which the page should be picked from. App is mandatory only if the app of the screen to be embedded and the app of the hosting page are different. screenid string - ID of the screen. Mandatory subscreenid string - ID of the subscreen. Mandatory. isTransactionShared boolean false If true, the hosting screen and the embedded screen will share the transaction. Else, transaction will be different for both the screens isSharemode boolean false If true, the hosting screen and embedded screen will share the mode. When mode is set via the controller for the hosting screen, the same screen will be set to the embedded screen as well and vice-versa. Else, the mode will not be shared. When set to the hosting screen, the mode will not be set to the embedded screen. tnmap Array<JSON> - An array of JSON with the keys fromtn and totn. The value of the keys should be the transnode relation ID of the host screen and embedded screen respectively. The transnode of the embedded screen will be added as a child to the transnode of the hosting screen so that when setActive is called on the parent transnode, data will be set on child. Example : [{"fromtn": "no_hdr_list", "totn": "detail_embedded"}] screenParameters INavToData This property expects a JSON the same as the navTo parameters. All the navTo parameters can be passed here. Flavor, Screen ID, subscreen ID, isTransactionShared, isSharemode and tnmap can also be passed as key-value pair here instead of separate properties.

If bound to a data field, the Tab control will always show whichever tab that field currently holds, and will keep showing it on subsequent loads/refreshes unless the field's value is explicitly reset. documents.t: onPageInit​ onPageInit hook method will be called only once as soon as the controller is loaded The transaction, model , and the UI is yet to be created for this, so those will not be available in this method. onPageModelReady​ onPageModelReady event will be called when the model is created and the transnodes are initialized, but the data is not set to the model yet. From this hook method developer can call skipModelPreparation method which will skip setting the data and executing the query. If the developer skips the model preparation, then developer should be responsible for setting the data is the model onPageEnter​ onPageEnter hook method will be called whenever the page enters the visible area by means of navigation(both forward and backward navigation). If the navigation is within the same page, this method will not be triggered onPageExit:​ onPageExit hook method will be called in the source page whenever the user navigates to a different page onPageDestroy: onPageDestroy hook method will be called only once when the page is destroyed. Page will be destroyed during the back navigation Example : if you are navigating back from PageB to pageA then PageB will be destroyed 14.1.1. TransNode API:​ Refer to this link for TransNode API. 14.1.2. Navigation API:​ Refer to this link for navigation API.

onValidate:​ If the transNode’s onarrive (in the transNode’s detail section) is provided as valid then, onValidate will be called during navigation. onAfterCreate:​ onAfterCreate method will be called once the new entity is created. onDelete:​ The onDelete method will be called once the entity is deleted.

Example: public set firstName(new\_value:string){ if(new\_value \== this.firstName) return; this.name:string \= new\_value\+" "\+this.lastName; this.s("firstName",new\_value,"string",false,false); } Getter function will be called whenever the entity property is getting read. The Where Used list can be accessed from the context menu of the following elements: Page Page Area Section Transnode To open the Where Used dialog: Right-click on the required element (Page, Page Area, Section, or Transnode). The context menu is displayed. Select Show Where Used from the menu. The Where Used dialog opens, displaying all references for the selected element. ​ When clicking on Show Where Used from the context menu, a Where Used dialog box opens. This dialog displays all references to the selected item within the current application. Dialog Layout​ The Where Used dialog is divided into two sections: Left Panel (Tree View) Displays a hierarchical list of all references for the selected item. Right Panel (Details View) Shows detailed information for the reference selected in the left panel. Selecting an entry in the tree view updates the details shown in the right panel. Supported Elements​ The Where Used feature is available for the following elements: Pages Page Areas Sections Transnodes Reference Checks by Element Type​ Pages The system checks for references in: Application menus Home pages Other pages (including embedded sections and tags) Associated files (controllers, utils) Navigation events within the current page (for example, navTo events) Page Areas The system checks for references in: Associated files(controllers, utils) NavTo Events, layouts in other pages and the current page Transnodes The system checks for references in: Binded data paths Associated files(controllers, utils) Navigating to Referenced Objects​ The Where Used dialog allows direct navigation to referenced application objects. In the left tree section, a Navigate button is displayed for application-level objects. When you click this button: A new tab opens automatically. The relevant tool or editor is loaded. The referenced object is preselected and highlighted in the opened tool.

For Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid section types, the Builder automatically applies horizontal alignment (hAlign) and text align property based on the control type and its associated binding. So the column header and the control will be aligned as per the standards based on the domain and control type Numeric Field Alignment​ If a control is bound to a property whose domain type is Integer or Decimal, the Builder automatically adds the hAlign config property and textAlign control property with the value Right. This automatic alignment is applied only when: The control is an input-based control. The control is bound to a property of domain type Integer or Decimal. Alignment Updates on Control Changes​ During updates, if: A control's value property or dsrc is modified, or A new binding is added to the control, the Builder automatically detects the bound property and updates the alignment accordingly.

This document helps the Application Team find the exact source of a query fired from a Procify application, optimize that query, trace the generated SQL, and use the relevant framework (FW) APIs efficiently. Details about Covers: locating the query source, query optimization techniques, enabling sufficient logging to inspect the generated query, and using FW APIs (e.g. addEndpoint) optimally.

Access to Procify Data Studio for the app/flavor under investigation. A working Private Node checkout of the application source (see the Private Node Setup guide). Access to Design Studio → Query Console (formerly SQL Executor). Access to Google Cloud Logging for the environment under investigation.

Not Applicable — the methods in this guide (Where Used List, Network Initiator, Private Node search, query logging) are built-in platform capabilities and do not require separate enablement. The optional logging flags are listed under Configurations below and Google Cloud Logging guide.

A. Finding the source of a query — Where Used List (Procify Data Studio)​ Open Procify Data Studio and select the App/Flavor that owns the entity or query in question. In the entity/query tree, locate the Entity, Query, Property, Value Help, or Event Exit you want to trace. Open the “Where Used List” option for that object. It lists every screen, query, rule, or event exit that references it, along with the property type / value help used where applicable. Use this list to narrow down which module(s)/screen(s) could be responsible for firing the query, before checking Network calls or code. B. Finding the source of a query — Chrome Network Initiator​ Open the application in Chrome and press F12 (or right-click → Inspect) to open DevTools. Switch to the Network tab, make sure recording is on, and clear existing entries for a clean trace. Reproduce the action in the application so the request fires. Find the relevant XHR/Fetch request (filter by “Fetch/XHR”). Click the request, then open the “Initiator” tab — it shows the call stack (exact file and line) that issued the request. Click any frame in the Initiator stack to jump to that source line in the Sources panel. C. Finding the source of a query — Private Node (Find in Folder)​ Set up / start your Private Node for the flavor in question. Open the application’s source checkout in VS Code, e.g. the src folder under the flavor’s workspace. In the Explorer, right-click the src folder → Find in Folder. Search for the query ID / entity ID / property name. Use “Match Whole Word” to avoid false positives. Review every places where this query/entity is used D. Optimizing the query​ Paste the query definition and surrounding code into an AI assistant (Recommended : Claude AI with Procify Knowledge Assistant) and ask for unnecessary joins, unused columns, and missing filters/indexes. Never paste real customer data or credentials. Apply setPartialSelect([...]) to return only the needed entity properties. Set setLoadAll(false) unless full-row data is genuinely required. Apply setLimit(n) Push filters into the query (setColumnFilter) instead of filtering in code afterward. Important: Expand All and an INNER JOIN on the same relation are not supported together — confirm which is configured before removing either. Re-run the optimized query in the Query Console and compare row counts / execution time. Query Console- User Guide Re-run the screen end-to-end on Private Node and capture a before/after timing as evidence. E. Using addEndpoint and other apis efficiently​ SN Steps 1 Call addEndpoint once per Business Object, not once per child entity — it already sends the full BO tree by default. 2 Leave onlydirtyobject at its default (true) to send only changed children; set false only when every child must be included. 3 Leave onlyRootEntity at its default (false) so children are included automatically. 4 Consolidate repeated addEndpoint calls against the same BO’s children into one call.

The following flags and settings control how much query/transaction detail is captured for debugging, without needing extra code. Parameter Description txn.enableStackTrace Boolean on the transaction (default false). Set true to record a stack trace of all activities of the transaction, including queries executed. Switch off again once captured. enableQueryStats Framework-internal flag (default true) driving query statistics collection. Do not disable unless instructed by platform engineering. "enableReqDump": true (klarion.json) Captures full incoming request payloads into the req_dump folder. Disabled by default. Turn off again after the investigation — req_dump folders have previously grown to multiple GB when left on. Select Distinct (Query → Detail) Set loadAll = true only when true column-level distinctness is required; otherwise leave Select Distinct off.

setPartialSelect​ setPartialSelect(entityPropertyNames: string[]): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description entityPropertyNames Array of return-entity property IDs to select, instead of every property on the return entity. setLoadAll​ setLoadAll(val: boolean): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description val Whether to load all fields of the return entity at execution time. Set false to skip properties/relations not required. setLimit​ setLimit(limitValue: number): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description limitValue Maximum number of records to fetch — use for pagination on list/search screens. setExpandAll​ setExpandAll(relations: string): string Parameter Description relations Comma-separated relation IDs to expand. Not supported together with an INNER JOIN on the same relation. addEndpoint​ addEndpoint(endpoint, type, channel, object?, onlydirtyobject?, onlyRootEntity?): EndPointBean Parameter Description endpoint Endpoint ID(s) to notify — meaning depends on type (BP_USER, ENDPOINT, USER). type EndpointType — determines how endpoint is interpreted. channel ChannelType filter on qualifying endpoints (default DEVICE). object The KloEntity whose full BO tree is sent. Defaults to the event object. onlydirtyobject Default true — only dirty child entities are included. Set false to force all children. onlyRootEntity Default false — children already included. Set true to send the root entity alone. Note: A single addEndpoint call already messages the root entity and its (dirty) children — avoid a separate call per child entity. getExecutedQuery​ getExecutedQuery(queryid, saveQueryObj, flavor?): Promise<KloEntitySet<KloEntity>> Parameter Description queryid Query name or entity name. saveQueryObj Saved query parameters to apply. flavor Optional — flavor to resolve the query/entity from.
